reviews.text: We celebrated a birthday in Scottsdale and were thrilled with The Phoenician.    Conveniently located to Old Town and great hiking at Camelback!    The amenities with the Spa, golf and the pool were amazing!    We will be back!
reviews.author: JordanC

reviews.text: My husband and I brought our family here for vacation the first week of March. We have three kids (6,5,2.5) and stayed in a casita by the pool. Our experience was five star. We’ve stayed at the ritz Carlton in grand cayman and the service and upkeep of resort was very similar. The food- outstanding. We got the salmon & cod dishes at Mowery and Cotton... it was fantastic. I ordered hummus and fish tacos by the pool more than once bc it was so good. Every single person there was kind, personable, and professional. I felt like the staff went above and beyond in making our vacation as relaxing as it could be. We will for sure be back again!
reviews.author: TheStevens

reviews.text:
Our stay at the Phoenician exceeded our expectations! My husband and I came to Scottsdale to celebrate our honeymoon. There were so many international travel restrictions that ultimately lead us to the Phoenician and it was such a blessing!

Your staff was incredibly accommodating. When we arrived we were a little let down with the view in our room and your staff switched our rooms with an amazing view, we will never forget those sunsets!!

My husband and I are both pescatarians. We looked at an outdated menu online and when we went there we realized there was not much that we were craving. The waitress (wish I remembered her name because she was AMAZING) asked us what we were craving, she went back to the chef and they made us a delicious salmon sandwich!  Little things like that mean so much!
They say the sense of smell is the strongest sense humans have. I will forever smell Byredo and think of my honeymoon! One of the friendly girls even gave me extras to take home!! I will definitely be asking my new hubby for their perfume!  
The food was to die for.... just check our receipt and you can see how much we loved the kabobs! Our only regret is that we didn’t try the watermelon jalapeño drink until the last day. 
The golf course was immaculate and my husband was giddy the entire day!
The spa treatment... OMGosh! We took advantage of all the spa amenities and felt so relaxed and connected the entire week!
We also played pickleball, basketball and took a walk almost every morning. This was an unforgettable trip and we cannot wait to return!
reviews.author: HoneymoonRerouted

reviews.text:
I can’t wait to return back for
An amazing stay at The Phoenician. Truly a top tier resort. The restaurant JG is a must when visiting.
reviews.author: LivBirthday

reviews.text: Such a wonderful resort! If you need a place to get away to work from a different home base during work from home times, it works ...or if you need a true vacation then it will satisfy that itch too. Our room was a nice size and very comfortable. The pools were great! The servers were on top of it from making sure we had towels to drinks. All of the restaurants at the resort were good with unique dishes and amazing flavors. We rented the bikes for a morning and explored the surrounding neighborhood and that was enjoyable. We will definitely stay here again.
reviews.author: Wayne Kimball, Jr.

reviews.text: Amazing customer service
reviews.author: Jason Garofalo

reviews.text: I just wrote a review, and it didnt post. Ugh.  Anyway nice hotel, but dont order room service. Hour and a half out for a resort is un exceptable.  Seem to not care.  Gold members but planted us next to service vehicle station.   Not really resort like.  We wont be back.
reviews.author: Daryn Bundy

reviews.text: Censasional
reviews.author: Maria Arredondo

reviews.text: GREAT service!  The grounds are beautiful and there is plenty to do on property.  Pools are great and precautions for distancing were comforting.
reviews.author: Midwestsnow2021

reviews.text: Absolutely Fabulous! What a gorgeous resort!
reviews.author: Sheri Abernathy

reviews.text:
Wanted to get away from the Midwest Winter for a couples vacation. 
 Great stay Feb 26-Mar 2 2021.  Beautiful resort. Great friendly service by every employee from the check-in clerk to the poolside servers.   Food was great throughout the entire resort: from poolside food, to breakfast at Mowry & Cotton to great views and dinner at J&G Steakhouse.  We had excellent weather as well which made our stay even better.  Would highly recommend.
reviews.author: JeffPChicago

reviews.text:
I just held a 2 day conference here. The view from the lobby bar (Thirsty Camel), the lovely piano playing from Allen, great chat from Chris, all pushed me over the edge to pick this place.

Fantastic rooms, gorgeous pools & cabanas, insane spa, and top notch convention center. Smiles and happy greetings for everyone.

Our attendees were blown away.

Wondering if our room was the nicest. Check out the Casita suites. They're crazy nice.
reviews.author: Brian Mason

reviews.text: We were given the worst room in the property after paying for an upgrade of the city view. The city was barely visible since we were on the first floor. Room service was taking too much time and certain items that I asked for like a firm pillow I got after staying 2 days in the hotel. First night they made me wait an hour for the pillows but still didn’t get it.
reviews.author: Anonymous

reviews.text: The Phoenician has it all.  Unbelievably gorgeous location...the grounds are so well maintained and designed.  The resort is set up against Camelback Mountain.  Take a stroll through the Cactus Garden Path.  Enjoy the views of the mountain from the lowest pool.  Everything is so well maintained.  The pool staff is attentive and friendly.  We enjoyed eating at Mowry and Cotton as well as at the pool.  The cocktails at the Thirsty Camel were excellent.  Love the location of the Phoenician as it is close to the mountain and so peaceful but a super short drive to the restaurants in Old Town.  We walked to old town during the day but didn’t want to walk with our heels on at night.  This resort is top notch.
reviews.author: Ilovetrips

reviews.text: Great location, grounds, and service. Amazing gym facilities and spa, pools were great, dining fantastic as well. Room showed a little bit of wear, but we spent most of our time enjoying the outside.
reviews.author: ORTraveler

reviews.text: This resort has many attractive features, including gorgeous public areas, stylish, clean and spacious rooms, friendly, helpful staff and excellent restaurants.  However, the swimming pools were quite disappointing, due to the pervasive loud music, which continuously played in every area.
reviews.author: AnthonyD

reviews.text:
Prior to my visit I had stayed at Hotel Grand Bretagne in Athens & Hotel Imperial in Vienna. Those experiences informed my perception of the Luxury Collection Brand; one that is synonymous with Refinement, Elegance, Attention to detail, yet warm and welcoming. 
My experience at the Phoenician was thus disappointing.
It is a well appointed hotel by all standards, but the service is poor. 
In some ways the vibe is that of Las Vegas Hotel wanna be, yet failing at that.  
Service feels 'mass produced' and rushed. No attention to detail. 
Front desk staff must be trained to be honest.
All style, yet no substance.
reviews.author: Gerald

reviews.text: Our family had an exceptional stay! The hotel is beautiful, restaurants were great, room was spacious and we felt safe and well taken care of.  What sets The Phoenician apart is the impeccable service. Every interaction we had from poolside service, dining service, room service etc. was above and beyond. We will definitely be back :)
reviews.author: CC

reviews.text: An beautiful resort to stay and to enjoy the many amenities offer.
reviews.author: Marianela Triana

reviews.text: Overall a wonderful stay.  Food, service, location and room were excellent.  My one frustration was the bed.  We stayed in the Phoenician Suite and the bed was so hard I couldn’t sleep throughout our stay.  Unfortunately, this is a fairly important component to a vacation.  My suggestion is to upgrade to a mattress that fits the luxurious environment of the room.  An significant oversight, but an easy one to fix.
reviews.author: Christy

reviews.text: amaiZing resort and amaiZing amenities! Love love love
reviews.author: Noushi

reviews.text: We visited the Phoenician for a well deserved rest.  The staff could not have been more friendly and helpful.  Wonderful people who obviously loved what they do.  The hotel was modern and updated.  Given the Covid situation,  the hotel was perfectly clean in every respect.  The food and drinks served there was of the highest quality.
reviews.author: Anonymous

reviews.text: Spacious rooms and bathroom however room phone didn't work and bathroom didn't lock so privacy was an issue.  Kids club is closed as well as the hot tub did to Covid restrictions.  Tennis courts were complimentary to play except you had to purchase the tennis balls!
reviews.author: LK

reviews.text: We always stay at Marriot properties for business travel..  This was our first experience in the Luxury Collection, and it was far from luxury.
reviews.author: ToddRomano

reviews.text: Everything about this hotel was fabulous! We had the hardest time leaving! From our beautiful breakfast looking out at the mountains, 5 star golf course, back to the pool for lunch and drinks, and then a wonderful dinner under the stars. We never left the hotel for 3 days.  Its the perfect getaway! Can't wait to go back. Thank you!
reviews.author: TamiCarinoCarbone

reviews.text: Our stay at The Phoenecian was exemplary!  Everything from the moment we checked in to the moment we left was perfect.  The room was ready and pristine. The service at the pool was fabulous as well as at the Rec center. Our meal at Mawry was extremely satisfying. There was nothing more that could have been done that wasn’t done.
reviews.author: KellyH

reviews.text:
My and I went to the Phoenician for our 40th wedding anniversary and decided to reserve a Casita as the advertisement on the websight looked amazing with the patios flowing out to the grass and sunrises and sunsets. So unfortunately here is a summary of our stay. 
Check-in was fine. We got to our "Casita" the front door was in a dark cave. The room was clean but dark, opened patio blinds to see an enclosed patio with a railing about 6 ft deep and just on the other side was a MAIN ACCESS ROAD for vehicles, delivery trucks and Golf course maintenance, on the other side of the road was a 3 story wall of the Golf course building! It was so loud we left. The worst was in the morning starting at 5:30am all morning long as the Golf course workers and delivery trucks started coming in like it was convention for them. So we never were able to sleep past 5:30am. Then we had no room cleaning that day. We called room service for 2 wine glasses that next evening an hour before we needed to leave for our dinner reservations to enjoy a special bottle we had brought. After 1 hour we needed to leave and still no wine glasses, as we opened the door to leave, the room service person was walking up with the glasses, before I could say anything he told me "I hope you are aware there is a $5 fee for the glasses". I said "well we won't be needing them now, we have to leave for dinner" he said OK, but that $5 still ended up on our bill. The other thing that's always kind of annoying is a Hotel that ads "Special Fees" on top of your room reservation like this hotel, a "Resort Fee $40" a "Self Parking fee $20"...it gives the appearance they are nickel & dimeing you, just build that in to the reservation. Resort was clean and pretty, but my advise to anyone staying is HAVE REGISTRATION SHOW YOU ON THEIR HOTEL MAP EXACTLY WHERE YOUR ROOM IS, as many rooms are dark and staring at nothing AND DEFINITELY DO NOT STAY ANYWHERE NEAR THE ACCESS ROAD TO THE GOLF CLUB.
reviews.author: WilliamR

reviews.text: A lovely hotel that afforded us a very nice winter escape.
reviews.author: Njw

reviews.text: I stayed here because of Gold Elit status with Bonvoy, but they’ll give you zero recognition and will not let you do a late check out! (I’ve stayed at the Ritz, the St Regis many times and they’ve all given me late check out, even in busy times)
reviews.author: Rafa

reviews.text: What a wonderful stay! Stayed at the Phoenician last weekend. We checked in late and there was a doorman that greeted us right away and assisted with our car and luggage. Check in process was smooth. The suite we were staying in was spacious and clean, there was a big patio with the wonderful view. Great staff everywhere at the resort, very welcoming and attentive. Kids had a lot at the water slide and a little water park, while my wife and I enjoyed a cabana at the pool. Don't forget to check out a beautiful cactus garden on the mountain side. Loved the food and drinks everywhere at the resort. Definitely will be back at this beautiful property!
reviews.author: ruslan khusainov

reviews.text: This resort epitomizes class, service, and quality. From arrival to departure, you and your reason for being there are the center of the staff’s attention. The golf course and restaurants were top class. So many amenities that we didn’t have time to fit them all in. We can’t wait to return!
reviews.author: Scott Thompson

reviews.text: If the Phoenician is going to present itself  as a luxury 5 star resort, it has some work to do. As I mentioned earlier it takes several times calling and being on hold to get through to someone. (Anyone, whether it is front desk or the concierge, athletic center). If you are  going to say breakfast is included, please know that $15 per person barely covers the coffee. Rooms are a little dated but clean. The front desk was “ho hum”, not very friendly. The best was the wait staff. There were some good things, Food at pool was excellent, Pickle ball court was great. IMO there are other resorts less expensive w/better customer service, and better rooms.
reviews.author: Anonymous

reviews.text: Horrible service and casitas need updating.
reviews.author: Akaye

reviews.text: A lovely luxurious resort with a superb golf course and breathtaking views.
reviews.author: Bruce Knoph

reviews.text: The service at the pool was slow and they forgot many items on our order. The rooms were a decent size but overly priced! The shower was extremely small to where the water was pelting you in the face and you had nowhere else to move. The room service was ridiculously expensive. This is a no frills resort with no activities for the kids. Just an average resort with outrageous prices! Can’t wait for the Ritz to open up!

reviews.text: Enjoyed a nice long President's weekend.  The property is stunning.  Grounds very well kept. Very nice staff. Felt very safe and appreciated during these terrible COVID times.
reviews.author: SMfromLA

reviews.text: we paid for a pool view room and had a view of a rooftop, hvac units, and a service entrance, but no pool in sight.

reviews.text: Simply amazing stay - it was our first time and probably not our last.
reviews.author: MacKenzieFamily

reviews.text:
Met family on Valentine's Day at their room..nice patio facing the pool. Staff is helpful and wears masks.
Enjoyed a walk through the cactus garden path.
Only complaint I heard was there were to many people at poolside considering Covid infection numbers in AZ.  However, this was only in the Holiday weekend.
reviews.author: May May Crafts wenk

reviews.text: This resort is an exceptional place. It is our new favorite resort to visit in Scottsdale. The rooms and hotel and grounds are impeccable. The staff is incredibly friendly and focused on providing outstanding customer service. The food and beverage quality was top notch. We loved being by the pools, walking the grounds, and enjoying conversation with staff. We will definitely be back!

reviews.text: Absolutely fantastic experience at Phoenician Scottsdale in early Feb and can't wait to go back.  We spent the week in a Casita with a lovely firepit.  The room was great, service throughout the visit was phenomenal, food was delicious, and the grounds were absolutely beautiful and really well maintained.  Location is perfect.  I just can't say enough good things about our time here!  I highly recommend!
reviews.author: HDuBois

reviews.text: Despite reservation glitch, Hannah squared things up very well.  Room service excellent!  Breakfast was delicious.
reviews.author: Matt Iverson

reviews.text: Being from Phoenix, this resort makes you feel as though you've left town. The views, the food, the drinks, the pools, the service- ALL top notch. We will definitely be coming back to staycation very soon!!
reviews.author: A

reviews.text: This is a stunning resort with beautiful views, grounds, pools, & rooms. The food was amazing, and the customer service was exceptional everywhere we went around the property. Can’t wait to return!
reviews.author: ErinE

reviews.text: Such a good time that ended too quickly. We will return.
reviews.author: sunseeker

reviews.text: Based on their website photos, we chose the casitas. Would not recommend that. They are very old and the price is very expensive for them. Not one bit worth it! I hope the hotel section has been updated to reflect the cost of the rooms. The restaurants are nice, the spa is very nice, the gym is exceptional. The casitas are horrible.
reviews.author: ErikaHeule

reviews.text: Five star resort for a reason
reviews.author: Adam F.

reviews.text:
This was a beautiful getaway backed up to camel back mountain where you can go on a nice hike. They have a gorgeous golf course, multiple swimming pools,  adult pool and cabanas. Pools are open 24hrs. Room service is impeccable with a nice menu.  There are shops in the hotel where you can buy designer sunglasses , swimsuits, and clothing .  You will find nothing but superb quality of service from the staff. You will find that the steakhouse is magnificent with an unbelievable view and sunset. (Make a reservation way ahead). They have a world known bar that comes with the most exquisite drinks made by top bartenders.
It is also minutes from the airport and downtown Scottsdale.
There is much more to enjoy and I will leave it up to you to explore.
I would like to give a special thanks to the staff for making my wife and myself feel like royalty!
Last but least an extra special thank you to Patrick & Kevin of the B&G Steak house and of course Jeff and Gennaro (aka Dr.G ) at the Adult pool and cabanas for your extraordinary service and pampering us on our anniversary.  Cheers 🍻🥂
reviews.author: J W

reviews.text: The resort is beautiful, very friendly staff, immaculate rooms and grounds, lots to do right at the resort. We never felt we had to leave to do anything except eat and only then because all restaurants were booked. We loved our stay. My only complaint was that upon booking we were guaranteed two connecting rooms with a city view. When we checked in the clerk said that the rooms had to be changed so we could have the connecting room and so we would get resort view rooms which would have been fine except the view was a turn around area for cars and another building. We were not in our rooms for long so I did not complain but my advice is that you insist on getting what your booking guarantee was unless it is an upgrade. Feel confident that you will have a wonderful stay in beautiful Scottsdale.
reviews.author: Susan

reviews.text: great service, friendly staff
reviews.author: SM

reviews.text: The staff was great, the resort grounds were spectacular, and the food was pretty good too. However as much as I enjoyed my time at The Phoenician, I detested the bathroom shower in our suite. Way too small! I felt like I was in a coffin.
reviews.author: JonniD

reviews.text: Our suite was dated, needed some upkeep.  A little over priced.  Staff was very attentive, grounds nice and well kept up, restaurants/food/service very good.  Probably would not go back due to the dated rooms.

reviews.text: Loved every moment at this beautiful property as did my 5# Yorkie Schatzi.

reviews.text: We had a very nice experience! Hotel staff was very nice
reviews.author: Meirklein

reviews.text: The Phoenician is a beautiful property with well kept grounds and beautiful views. The hotel is spread out over a larger property so prepare to walk. It’s like a vegas hotel, with everything you need on the property (shops + restaurants). Our room was nice with a partial view. We did have an issue with the showers water pressure and temperature which was not completely resolved. That was disappointing, especially for a five diamond resort.
reviews.author: HAlem

reviews.text: Absolutely amazing place to stay. The resort is massive. There is a beautiful cactus garden, beautiful pool, and unreal golfing experience. The rooms are large updated and clean. Beds are extremely comfortable. The staff are friendly and professional. You can easily call in Uber/Lyft to get into town for reasonable prices. Highly recommended.

reviews.text: Great Resort with fabulous attentive staff. There is reason why this is a 5 star resort!

reviews.text: Room was great/modern, bar was vibrant. Great breakfast spot, great coffee shop.

reviews.text: Would never stay at this hotel again or recommend it to anyone

reviews.text: Just got back from a golf trip w/friends at the Phoenician and couldn't recommend the hotel high enough.   We had excellent service at all times before and during our stay.  Our rooms, the restaurants, golf course and spa were all top notch.   Can't wait to go back!

reviews.text: Our stay at the Phoenician was wonderful. We had a great time and loved all the staff. We were very impressed by the excellent customer service and the staff was always ready to make your experience the best. The price of the room may be on the higher side and some of the resort can use some updating, however the people make the difference.

reviews.text: We have been able to travel a bit during this pandemic and have not found any other Resort or Hotel to have such a happy atmosphere.  The staff we encountered were ALL extremely helpful and pleasant.  It gives hope in times like this!!

reviews.text: I had just got married and we decided to have a mini honeymoon to enjoy the rest of our weekend. The stay was absolutely perfect. We requested room service to be in our room prior. We enjoyed the drinks at the thirsty camel in which our server was amazing as well. In the evening we had dinner at J&G, we didn’t think to make a reservation but they were still able to accommodate us with a nice table in the bar with a view of the pool. Overall all staff we encountered was great.

reviews.text: Great property, golf views from course were fantastic.  Service was superior.
reviews.author: JamesKelly

reviews.text: Beautiful hotel, great service. Loved the pool, what a resort.

reviews.text: I took a yoga class there from a Metta yoga instructor.  The class and the setting were amazing. Zach, the instructor, expertly guided us through a fabulous flow. It was so peaceful to practice next to Camelback Mountain in an oasis garden. I highly recommend it!

reviews.text: not very pleasant, the staff was far from nice and my room wasn't the cleanest.
reviews.author: Washington G

reviews.text: Afternoon tea with a few dear friends, while the food was nice and the pianist was amazing, the options for tea where a select few. Once you ordered that was all that you were offered. I've been to tea other places and they are more than happy when you ask for different ones each time with hopes if there is one that you really enjoy you are more like to take some home as well. Seated next to the door going out to the balcony with a view was nice, however, the door was left open with a rather chilly breeze coming in on me the majority of the time and never was asked if it was fine or not. Honestly expected more for the price and location.
reviews.author: First name

reviews.text:
We had a wonderful time at The Phoenician. The guest room and amenities were fabulous. The cactus garden was beautiful lit up at night and a pleasure to walk and explore during the day. The breakfast buffet at the golf center was provided in a safe ( precautions during during covid) manner with great delicious selections. Our New Year
‘s Eve dinner was fabulous as well. Staff friendly and facilities very clean. We are  forward to a longer stay where we can partake in the multi level pools,   tennis, and what looks like a great athletic center. Enter  We chose a great place to say goodbye to the dreadful year of  2020 and hello to a hopeful 2021!
reviews.author: TheMortonFamily

reviews.text: Every thing about the Phoenician is luxury, friendly, accommodating and relaxing. Great place to stay.
We will be returning. I don't have a single complaint. Literally everything was amazing, I give everything a 10!

reviews.text: The location is great. I booked a garden view room directly with the hotel and had a view of the restaurant. I asked to change rooms but was told they were booked. reviews.text: Would have gave 5 stars but the pool was not heated n jacuzzi was closed, basically ruined my staycation, the excuse was COVID-19 But other hotels ive stayed at in the area around this time still had their pools and jacuzzi running normally, if thars the case I think their rooms should be discounted, not worth the money.
reviews.author: Nyla Goddess

reviews.text: Comfortable bed, friendly staff, limited food options at the moment. Beautiful grounds and swimming pools.
reviews.author: Michael Smith

reviews.text:
I graciously give this resort 3 stars simply because I am visiting during COVID and the room was at least comfortable. It certainly did not feel like even that good of an experience.

We checked in late due to some travel delays, and the staff was mostly courteous and helpful.

We went to Mowry & Cotton for breakfast and waited 25 minutes for a table. They did space seating out a bit, which I appreciated due to Covid. We then waited another 20 before a server greeted us, brought water, anything. Our food took another 45 minutes, I had to beg for a coffee refill, and with two kids...we were exhausted/frustrated by the time we left. But even so, we returned to this restaurant 4 more times during our stay...as it’s the only choice on property. None of our subsequent visits were better. In a nutshell: service consistently slow beyond belief, also begged for a second glass of wine with dinner, food subpar, way overpriced for a terrible experience time after time. The final lunch, we had such a hard time getting service, birds swept in and onto our table to scavenge scraps that were not bussed. It was shocking!

The Phoenician Spa was the worst I’ve been to. Do NOT waste your precious time or money! The locker room was so busy, on a Sunday, I felt like I was at the YMCA at rush hour. The facial (Farah) was a joke where they amateurishly tried to push product on me. I then had a pedicure with Fannie who did not seem very well trained. They force you to sign your check with a 20% gratuity BEFORE your services...and now I see why! I had to return the next afternoon to have my polish redone (which took an additional 45 minutes AFTER I waited 2 hours for someone to do it) due to it pooling up in clumps like a child had done it. I appreciated the lady fixing it, but at this point I felt like I was part of a game in the Twilight Zone of “resorts,”  everything taking 10x longer than it should!

Regarding the property as a whole, there is a lot of disrepair, to the point my husband and I compared it to the crumbling facade of Vegas. The shops have extremely limited inventory- all XS sizes in dresses and no shirt sizes for my boys either. I asked & they said they only had the 2 kids’ XL that we’re hanging on the rack. The ladies in the shop addressed my husband and other customers as “Bud,” as in “ready, Bud?” after they treated us like thieves as we browsed. As I write this, I might add we look very “normal,” have never been treated like this in my life (not that I think it’s right to profile). In fact, since we are Platinum Elite within Bonvoy/Marriott, we are usually treated quite well. They were rude to another lady who wanted to buy a drink or something & they curtly said “ten dollar minimum!” Near the shops, there is a small market where I spent $24 on a breakfast sandwich & coffee one morning, and I stood there for twenty minutes even though I was the only one waiting!

My boys enjoyed the pools, but we had a hard time getting service the second day we were there, to the point my husband went to the (ahh! M&C again!- that was our dreaded 4th time but kids were starving) restaurant to order food. I even asked the pool “manager” for service, and he said he’d send someone “right away.” No one came. It definitely started to feel like a joke, like we were on Punk’d or something. We could not wait to leave.

reviews.text:
EDIT TO ADD: I have received follow-up as seen below and personally from the Phoenician, so they do care about their service standards, and that is worth noting.

This was definitely NOT a 5 star experience and worth the cost.

We arrived for a Staycation on Friday at 11am and were told check-in was not until 4pm. We requested an early check-in because we had dinner plans at 5p and needed to get ready. We were told that should not be a problem and we would be called when our room was ready. We went to hang at the pool and service there on Friday was very good (food and service was excellent). Around 1p I called to check on the room and was told they were working on the floor our room was at and it shouldn't be much longer. Having not heard anything I ended up calling at 2p, 3p, then again at 3:30p as we started to worry we would not be able to get in to shower and get ready. I decided to to go the front desk, where I again had to wait in an extended line and by the time we got to the desk it was already 4p, but our room was still not ready. I let the desk clerk now that was not acceptable and they mentioned they would get as a room. Not an enjoyable experience.

The next day breakfast by the pool was excellent, but as we settled into the pool area for the day we found the service was, well...non-existent in our area (adult pool west side). I was literally with a few hundred feet of the service area and could well have walked there myself to get food and drink instead of waiting up to 20 minutes for our server to appear (we are talking 20 minute to see her and order, then another 15 minutes or much more to even get it). She did mentioned she had a larger area, but would be by often. That was not the case. Once I got up to find out where our order was (I walked and had to find her to remind her we ordered), once I had to send one of the pool attendants to find her, and then finally I did mention we need a little more prompt service, and she again apologized, but disappeared again for another 20 minutes. When she did finally show with our drinks I just told her to please QUICKLY get us a check and we didn't need the last order. Was just not a relaxing or attentive experience for what the Phoenician is supposed to bring as a high-end resort. There was another server doing the whole rest of the adult pool and he would be by several times in the time it took our server to show up once.

The resort was not that busy.

So some really good, but also some very unacceptable poor service. 5 star resort? You can get better service for much less. Check out Valley Ho or any number of places right around Scottsdale.

reviews.text:
Came on a romantic trip for my wife and I. I booked a king suite... we checked in at 430 since check in was at 4p. With all the excitement of being at one of the best resorts in Arizona we couldn’t wait to get to the room! We got to the room and it was nice got to our bed and it was a double queen bed!!! I am 6’3 and pay the extra because I wanted this to be comfortable and nice for my wife! I called and the manager said “sorry nothing we can do!” I asked to speak to the manager and his response was “you’re speaking to him!” With him speaking to me rudely I kept my cool and said I needed something better. He said he has one that will be free but won’t be available until 8-9p I said that was fine since we will be going to dinner. We come back 800-830ish and get a room great!! No not great non of the lights worked from the wall and A/C was off and when it’s 116 degrees it’s was hard to get the room cool. Here’s the top of that .... I open the fridge to put my water in and it had the previous guest open, eaten, food and other items in there. Both the bell boy and hospitality guy said it was bad and apologized. I spoke with another manager because the other one left...she will very nice and calm. At this point it was 930ish and my wife was ready for bed (there goes the fun right?!) she offered to put us in a regular room and comp us $150 great but the only thing is our room on the king suite was $580 more a night (2 nights) and $150 isn’t going to do anything. She said give her a moment and she will see what she can do...

She calls back and gets us into a presidential suite!! Awesome never been so I said that’s great!! Takes the comp away from me and I said ok? Get to the room and yup QUEEN BEDS!  And I’m the master suite queen! At this point it’s 10-1030 and we are just over it and said forget it last time we are here just enjoy the spa...

Spent $1300 at the spa tipped the pool boy $100 and the nail tech $100 , bell boy $50 and took care of anyone who serviced my wife and I. Spa was great! Came back to the room at 445 to get ready for dinner and our room wasn’t touched no house cleaning new towels non. Didn’t call just waiting for check out .

I’m so done with this place and how they can’t get to an idea on how to make it right other than sorry nothing we can do! The resort isn’t cheap for those who are fortunate enough to afford it but it’s not about the money it’s the principle and how someone who works hard for his money to enjoy things he pays for only to get the worse service! I can see if this was a motel 6 but it’s one of the highest rated resorts!!! Definitely upset and hope someone from corporate will call or contact me about this!! I have pictures to prove my claims as well as video

I was really excited about this staycation. However, as soon as we checked in we had learned that the left hand was not talking to the right hand. Initially at registration, and on a call to reserve our room, we had been told that the game room was open from 11-6. On day two when we asked about the game room we were told it was closed.
We scheduled appointments at the spa and the girl on the phone told us that spa closed at 6pm. Scheduled our appointment for 4:00pm and when we were done with our massage, we were excited to go to the rooftop pool only for the staff to tell us it closed at 5. There was no steam room or sauna, and when I asked for a discount because of we had fewer amenities, the girl was rude and said that “none of the other clients had a problem with the price.” Uhm, I’ve been to PLENTY of resort spas with ALL amenities included have never had to pay 200 a person for a massage with NO AMENITIES.

reviews.text: Tea time at the Phoenician is that special treat for my wife. I make the reservation and place it in her google calendar. Not long after a surprise kiss comes back in my direction. Day of the reservation involves getting cleaned up and dressed up. Slacks, nice polo and my Allen Edmond dress shoes. She goes all in. Flowing dress, full makeup and jewels. Hit the Phoenix art museum for a couple hours then it's off to tea time. We arrive to be seated by the professional friendly staff. Choose our teas from the menu. I love the variety of finger sandwiches. Sipping tea and soaking in the atmosphere while pianist plays for our pleasure. When you had your fill of finger sandwiches plating is taken away. Scones arrive on new plates with devonshire cream and choice of jam. Unwinding with your significant other while viewing the beautiful landscaping through floor to ceiling windows. Then the plates are removed again while deserts are brought to the table being the final course to tea time. This is the best tea time in Arizona

My visit to the Phoenician was one of the best experiences I have ever had at a resort.
The service wasn't just excellent, the people who work there are so pleasant and helpful, and treat you as if they love what they do and enjoy people. Far different from the robotic obligatory attention at other places.
Everything was sparkling clean.
There is plenty to do here, but if you don't feel like doing any of it you can enjoy some coffee or wine on your private balcony. Mine overlooked a natural area.
The cactus garden is beautiful, and I enjoyed a wall along the paths on the grounds.
There was even a falconer walking around, falcon hooded, to keep crows away from guests and food.
The resort is large, it never felt noisy or crowded. There are adult only pools but I did not notice any or many kids. Nighttime was peaceful, no noise to keep me up.
The ambience here invited fun relaxation.
I will be visiting again soon.

reviews.text:
As a celebration of the birth of baby #6 of our group and reunion of life-long friends on opposite coasts, my best friend reserved a mom's night out stay on Saturday at the Phoenician. After a nice dinner and massages in the morning, the next day took a negative turn and resulted in us having to leave around 10am to pick up the kids and take our friend's dog to the emergency vet.

Upon check-out, we asked if we could return another day, as we were planning to originally stay and enjoy the amenities for most of the afternoon.  A sweet voice named Monica greeted us from Concierge services and confirmed that the resort would offer us a day pass on Tuesday and that email confirmation would be sent.

When Tuesday arrived with no email receipt, we called the resort.  After being put on hold for nearly 30 minutes, we proceeded to be passed to multiple representatives all denying the day pass.  Eventually, a manger named Andrew confirmed Monica made a mistake.

Instead of offering ANY consolation for the resort's error, they proceeded to demand we rebook another night stay.  After 30 more minutes of explaining/crying from our new mom-of-3 friend, Andrew did not budge and condescendingly said to come to the hotel if we wanted to figure it out.

All three of our friends made the 45 min drive to find Andrew at the front desk.  In addition to the lack of eye contact or any mention of apologies and sympathy for the situation, he instead blankly asked for ID and form of payment.

As the wife of a Titanium Elite Marriott member who travels extensively for work, my friend was heartbroken that not only was her one day of rest taken away from us but that there nothing the resort offered to do to help for someone who has spent hundreds of thousands of dollars at this chain.

We're all disappointed in the Phoenician's management and can't wait to take our money to the Hilton brand from now on.

(Note, the pools staff including Hannah, Heather and Pam were fantastic and should receive five out of five stars!)

Beautiful place! I was here for a work conference for 4 days and I enjoyed every moment. The meeting rooms, the catering, the guest rooms and the activies. They did a little of everything.

The grounds were clean and well kept. The design was modern and equipped with all of the amenities you could want. Golf, fitness center, tennis courts and walking distance to Camelback Mountain for hiking.

Whether you have in-room dining, you enjoy one of the many insight restaurants or catering for your event, the food was superb. Everything was cooked to perfection and the buffet tables were always replenished.

I was here for work but could definitely see myself coming back for recreation with my family.

reviews.text:
My company hosted our annual meeting here for our top clients and the Phoenician did not disappoint. From pulling through the resort gates, to the beautiful grounds and the ease of check-in, I new this would be a special event. They helped us host game night, provided food in a timely manner that was always delicious and beautifully presented. The staff always greeted us and regardless of their role, was willing to help us in any way they could. 

While my room was a good ways from the convention space, it was a still quite pleasant. I passed the hall of shops where you could by apparel, coffee and more. I also passed the main lobby where there were always people gathered enjoying the bar and great conversation. The elevators were extremely high tech where you make your floor selection from outside the elevator. We all thought that was pretty smart but it doesn't stop you from looking for buttons inside. 

As you walk towards your room, you notice a glass door closing off the public space from the rooms. This way you keep the noise down. Upon entering the my room, I was very impressed. There was a hallway with two separate closets a bathroom on suite with a separate shower, a soaked tub and and private toilet stall. 

The room was huge with an over-sized king bed, a sitting area and a table for in room dining. There was also a mini-fridge equipped with not only alcohol mini's but soft drinks, Gatorade, red bull and more. As a new mom, I needed an additional refrigerator for milk, a simple call to the front desk and the fridge was delivered in less than 15 mins. 

I would definitely come back to this place. Hopefully, for leisure next time.

Unfortunately, I did not have a nice stay here. The number of things that went wrong here were too many- overbooked restaurants for hotel guests, hair in tub, no room cleaning while out of the rooms (they only came when we were in our rooms trying to relax), housekeeping staff were loud and rude, concierge NEVER got back promptly and didn't ask or get back to you about what was asked but what they wanted to, perks of hotel like bike rentals and tennis courts were NEVER available, they shut down things without notice (i.e. tea service), internet constantly booting devices off, staff is a bit snooty, inconsistent information from staff, etc.

My guess is that this hotel caters to locals and their needs so if you are an out of town guest without the big bucks to get their attention, you may be disappointed. In a survey, I wrote: "There are places that cater to the wealthy and do not care about others. Then there are places that cater to their customers, wealthy or not."  In my experience, this was not a place that catered to their customers...

reviews.text:
The Phonecian, Luxury collection resort has been on my bucket list for a while. Located in Scottsdale Arizona, its a very exclusive luxurious resort with plenty of amenities, beautiful views, great dining, and amazing rooms. It will be about a 30 min drive from the airport, but not far from many places in Scottsdale if you do want to leave.

There's a guard shack to get in, though it can't be hard since ubers get in all the time. You drive to the end for reception, passing by a massive sports complex on the left (which I didn't get toenjoy but looked amazing). Reception is in a beautiful lobby overlooking the resort that compares closely to any Ritz, St. Regis, or other 5 star property. Think swanky furniture, mood lighting, and luxury touches. Check-in was quick and easy, and off I went to my Casitas suite (thank you suite night awards).

The suite was absolutely amazing with a kitchenette, dining table, living room with plenty of seating, 2 Full Baths (seriously, with 2 sets of soaking tubs and showers), and a humongous master bedroom thats bigger then most hotel rooms. Patios overlooking the pool complex completes the room. Frette slippers were just some of the finer touches you don't see even at most 5 star resorts.

The pool complex was amazing as well, and since this was winter not crowded at all. If you're in the casitas you will have to walk through them to get to the main complex again (highly recommend dining at Mowry & Cotton)

This is not a cheap property, but worth every penny. Needs to be on everyones bucket list.

reviews.text: I’ve wanted to visit this property for many many years and finally had the opportunity to in Nov 2019.  The renovated rooms were gorgeous and did not disappoint!  The service at our conference was shockingly poor.  The breakfast buffet was always well staffed and had the best food.  Lunch was average and dinner service was surprisingly poor.  One dinner meeting didn’t have enough food for our tables of 10 that were setup.  I can’t believe that lower quality food and restaurant service is the norm and we had to of been there at just the wrong time for that to happen.  Despite that, I’d go again because it was simply beautiful and would bet the food and service was an anomaly this time.

reviews.text: We attended Christmas Camp at the Phoenician with friends. The resort was beautifully decorated - and the staff were exceptional. The Christmas Camp weekend was well-planned and a delight to participate in. The cactus garden was lit up with Christmas lights, making for a fun walk. The ability to take golf carts around the resort made it very easy to be delivered to different activities around the resort - and to enjoy dinners at other restaurants outside the main building. Our room was spacious, impeccably clean, and the beds were cozy and very comfortable. We will definitely plan to stay at this resort in the future.

reviews.text: Superb stay while attending a confernce.  We enjoyed the amenities and were thrilled with the level of consistent service we received. We stayed with our 2 children (3 + 6) and they were beyond thrilled with the activities that were available to them. We enjoyed the fact that this resort welcomes families but does not feel like a 'family resort'. The dining options were plentiful, the pool area was fabulous and the location is in close proximity to Old Town Scottsdale. We would absolutely stay here again with our family but also look forward to returning on a adult/couples only trip. My only 'complaint' is that you have to completely empty the mini-fridge in the room in order to use it (as it comes fully stocked with all sorts of snacks and beverages). We had some fruit and light snacks for our children and my efforts to have the mini-fridge emptied and collected for our personal use came unanswered by hotel staff so the contents of the fridge were taking up space on the dresser and looked unsightly.

reviews.text: The wife and I stayed here for four nights over Columbus Day weekend.  We liked everything about this place.  Our room was spacious and modern, although we didn't have a great view - we overlooked the driveway leading up to the main entrance.  The pool areas are nice - we had no trouble getting lounge chairs under the umbrellas. The small restaurant near the pool had very good fish tacos.  We ate at the Marketplace every morning. Here you can get a quick breakfast to go which we ate at the outside tables overlooking the fountain near the hotel entrance.  The hotel is next to Camelback Mountain and behind the hotel is a very beautiful and unusual cactus and sculpture garden.  The fitness center looks brand new and has the latest equipment, including Peleton bikes.  My wife enjoyed her massage at the spa.  They have a terrific tennis facility. I took two lessons with Niles - a great tennis instructor - I highly recommend.  Service at the hotel is top notch - they have a great staff.  I used the Bonvoy app one evening to request more toilet paper and it was delivered in under five minutes. Very impressive.  The hotel is located only about 10 minutes by car from the Old Town area of Scottsdale which has many art galleries and great restaurants.  We can't wait to come back here. Go.

reviews.text:
Beautiful hotel. Customer service and attention to detail is lacking. Had to ask for a coffee cup the first day- after waiting for quite a while they show up with everything but the cup.
Had a misunderstanding with housekeeping and the manager came by and offered us a credit, which we appreciated but it seems they’re severely understaffed. I felt terrible for the housekeeping staff.
Drinks at the pool are a joke. We asked for an extra shot and were charged $14 for the drink, $14 for the extra shot, and were still left wondering if it had alcohol in it after dropping $28 on it.
Ordered lattes at 4 am and was told it’d take 20 min... 45 min later and they show up with cold lattes that were more milk than anything.
The spa was nice, however if you show up early to do the “pre-treatment ritual” you’ll want to wear a watch. They have one clock in the area and you can’t see it from the majority of the pre-treatment area. Kind of hard to relax when you have to worry about the time and going downstairs to meet your massage therapist. I’ve been to spas that charge $120/hr and have natural hot springs baths that were more attentive than this. I’m used to getting in the pools/baths/steam rooms, etc. and being asked by the attendant what time my appt is. They ALWAYS tell me to relax and enjoy and they’ll worry with the time and come get me when it’s time to get ready for my massage. That is relaxation.
I was never asked about allergies or asked to fill out paperwork and the only lotion they had was full of things I’m allergic to if they come into contact with my face. Very odd experience.  The massage was nice.

We also smelled something that resembled sewage or feces in the parking garage and by the restaurants.

reviews.text:
Just returned from the best getaway! Goodness the Phoenician surely doesn’t disappoint! I have been to very few places that have the customer service skills these ladies and gents shower you with, if you have a problem they have a solution! In fact you don’t even have to have a problem and they still make you feel like they’ve came up with a solution. My husband and I went out for a hike one morning, we returned and while walking down the hallway to our room the kindest man said “mam, can I get you some ice and a few bottles of water”
then offered to deliver it to our room. Seriously, we stayed here for 5 days and experienced this kind of service multiple times a day. reviews.text:
If it's beauty I'm reviewing I'd give a 5++.
Hubby & I took a quick stay~cation for the July 4th weekend and felt  Bliss & Paradise until right before check out.
Standard checkout is 12pm but we asked for a late check out 2pm.  We were granted this request via my pre~check in phone call  (Ryan) and reconfirmed at our physical check-in (Ryan-front desk). Sunday morning before brunch I called the front desk to confirm for the 3rd time a 2pm checkout.
Initially we had a 2nd floor room overlooking the pool and had to move to the ground with a a garden view which was even more beautiful due to hip issues for me.  The team was very understanding and while we were out of the room they moved our belongings to the new room making such an impression on us as far as their level of customer service and accommodations made to us.
After we enjoyed our amazing beautiful brunch at Mowry & Cotton, we wanted to enjoy a couple hours at the pool before spending our last hour in the room for privacy and to take advantage of the beautiful HUGE tub for a relaxing bubble bath and music.  10 minutes after 1pm a maid entered our room without knocking catching my husband pulling up his underwear & me still in the tub.  My husband asked if she even saw the privacy marker which she replied, "YES”  and left.
35 minutes later and 15 minutes before 2pm a knock at the door this time asking if we were still in the room and a statement that we were showing gone.
Instantly we loaded our bags & exited the room, headed straight to the front desk (Kamden) to share our experience.  Kamden showed no empathy for the embarrassment endured by my husband and reluctantly credited us our $35 resort fee after I explained how the last hour ruined our whole experience & our embarrassment has no value.
I can't believe that after confirming 3 times we still had an issue.

reviews.text:
From all the Luxury Collection Hotels that we had stay around the word (Dubai, Indonesia, France, Mexico among others) this has been the one with the lowest service attention. 

We arrived after a long day of flights , around 11pm for check-in and we were questioned with the “rate” that we got for the hotel stay (A rate that my husband uses as a consultant for that company and I previously did too). The person at the front desk didn’t even took attention to our elite status (we are both Platinum) so no upgrade was provided. When I asked they mentioned the gift or points but didn’t give us an introduction of the facilities and events the hotel offers. The room assigned to us had a view to a concrete wall. BTW I heard another guest complaining to the front desk about the customer serviced offered by the person who also checked us in.

That night we notice a cricket on our jacuzzi tub. My husband decided to take out alive instead of calling the desk and killing it. A hotel at this level and rate should be paying more attention to details like this.

The next morning we proceed to play golf at their course and this turn out to be amazing! Great attention and great course. KUDDOS to the golf department and the people on the serving carts for all the detailed attention!

We had a good time too at the pool (we were in the adult pool). The pool area is very nice, what I would recommend is more waiters around the area to speed up taking orders. The hotel easily lost 2-3 additional drinks that we could had purchase if we they had more waiters to request these too. Also, towels were nit available when we went and had to get them later after we were already at the pool. 

The lobby area and bar is great! We had time to drink, eat and chat at the lobby bar with Raul and Chris. Great guys and nice chats. We got recommendations of places to go at night around Old Town.

In summary we will definitely return to the golf course and hangout in the lobby bar but not stay at the hotel. The service was not what we have experienced on other  luxury collection hotels or the treatment we have received as a lifetime Gold guest becoming lifetime Platinum.
reviews.author: Jill

reviews.text:
Did not stay at the hotel but the afternoon tea is worth the price of admission (free)! A beautiful big lobby that reminds you of a Vegas hotel yet in another dessert. Stunning view of greens.

The service was impeccable the moment we walked up to the host stand. Then the menu was composed of combos options and depending how hungry you are you can do the bare minimum or a full smorgasboard of sandwiches and desserts.

Each server walks by and you can have your fill of sandwiches and when you have had your fill then you can move onto dessert. Similar to the sandwiches there are a plethora of choices.

Even if you aren't staying here the public areas are fun to walk around. The gift shops have fun items and the coffee shop also serves great items. Overall a great place to visit for a short or long time.

Really expensive resort.  So many additional charges per night it was insane.   It came out to nearly $350 per night!

Tried cocktails at multiple bars throughout the property, stick to the basics because the specialty cocktails are terrible.

Food was average, I think the kitchen really enjoys red onions because basically every dish had them.

I had a charge of $65.47 attached to my hotel bill from 11/17/17 for lunch at a restaurant on the property while I was on a plane headed back home that took 3 months to resolve.  Countless phone calls and voicemails left for accounting and no one returned even one of my calls.  How did I fix it you ask?  I had to dispute the charge with my credit card company because The Phoenician didn't feel like refunding me.  They were too busy to return my calls.

There are better resorts in the area that are not only a better value but provide better service.  The stay, food and beverage and the grounds were just ok.

reviews.text: We visited Scottsdale for the first time this year and were looking for a relaxing, luxury resort with breath taking views. After researching it seemed as if The Phoenician was just that. |IT ABSOLUTELY WAS. |Upon checking in the staff treats you like royalty and goes above and beyond. |We stayed in a 3 bedroom residence with plunge pool. I cannot rave about this stay enough!!!!! |Beautiful large house that can accommodate a large party if needed but also great for a relaxing couples stay. Would be excellent and more than enough space for a large golf group. I was pleasantly surprised at a small office with computer printer etc in this residence too!|Beds are extremely comfortable. |Large closet spaces. |The master shower is oversized and so luxurious. |Kitchen has all pots, pans, appliances if you want to cook during your stay but room service is delicious and worth it if you decide to go that route. |We had our own small private pool with breath taking views. I really didn’t even need to leave the residence if I didn’t want to!!|I did however venture up to the main property. They did provide us a golf cart to drive up to the main property but honestly the views were so pretty I ended up choosing to walk to the fitness center, spa, and main Phoenician pool with no problem!|The fitness center is huge. Two stories. Brand new. All the equipment you could want or need. TVS everywhere. Absolutely a luxury amenity. |The spa was amazing too. I had an 80 min massage and it was one of the best I’d ever had. The staff at the spa are top notch making you feel extremely welcome and at home. |We ventured up to the main resort area to the pools and had a great time. There are a few different pools and bars! We hung out at the adult only pool which was nice but if you have children with you there’s plenty of pool area for them to enjoy too! If you’re looking for easy and quick poolside snacks the flatbread quesadilla was very, very good. ||The views at this resort are absolutely amazing. It doesn’t get much better than this. |We enjoyed our stay so much we went back two weeks later to the Phoenician and stayed at the Canyon Suites this go round. ||I cannot say enough good things about The Phoenician. No matter if you choose The Residence, Canyon Suites, or rooms on the main property you absolutely cannot go wrong at this resort. If you’re looking for breathtaking views and a luxurious stay with activities such as golf, tennis, spa..... this is it. Worth the splurge for sure!|

reviews.text:
A great location and their Concierge desk without exception is absolutely amazing!!!!

The service from the hotel guest service department however, is severely lacking!!!!!!

An example of horrible service: I forgot my toiletry kit in my room upon check out. While not the hotels fault in anyway, I called and they retrieved it for me. I had moved hotels for the night as I was on a business trip inspecting other properties after my conference.

I asked if they could send it to me down the street (approx 10 minutes by car - $6.50 by Lyft or Uber).  They said no problem and asked how I wanted to pay the $130.00 charge for sending it.  I was told that they could only send it by limo that charged by the hour and there was no other option. I called Lyft, who then picked it up from the concierge for me and delivered it to me at my new hotel. Total cost for me approx $12.00.

Just think of the good will they lost out on and what the review would have been like had they actually thought outside of the box. I recommend hotels because of the service they provide my guests!  This is not a hotel I will ever recommend because of the shortsightedness they had.

I am first to say that it is too bad, that such a beautiful hotel in a great location, failed so miserably at their customer service.

Had a company outing this evening. My guest and I could not find our way to the ballroom where the event was held as the place is huge. I was hungry and our company had fried food apps that I was not interested in even though it was our annual awards ceremony. I was told that we could go to the Tavern on-site. I was so frustrated after waiting for 10-15 minutes that I went to the room and ordered room service. It is now 11 pm and I have still not had dinner yet. I am a foodie and am well traveled. I am not impressed with the resort and don't expect to return. Save your money and stay at a 4 star resort instead. Overall,
I was hoping to have one evening in which to celebrate w/o any

reviews.text: I will start off by saying that the property is gorgeous. The only issue that we had was the treatment we received. We were here with a large group for a total of four days. We enjoyed the many amenities offered by the property. Most of the staff were extremely kind and courteous. However we did experience a few occasions where we were made to feel not welcome. The first incident was when we visited the pool. The young lady went around to each guest to ask them what they would like and skipped us. Eventually we moved from the jacuzzi area to the pool. We selected our lounge chairs and proceeded to swim. The young lady still had not acknowledged us. It started to rain. We rushed over to our area to put up the umbrella as our things were getting wet. The young lady finally came over to help but we had been there for quite some time and at this point we just took the interaction at face value. She finally asked what we wanted and we ordered and that was that. The next incident came the next day during afternoon tea. I made reservations in advance. We arrived about 10 minutes early. There was no direction on what to do or where to go so we chose seats we felt were appropriate. I realize our mistake so that is not the issue. The issue came when the hostess came over and told myself and the guest I was with was that the seats were reserved for the afternoon tea. She automatically assumed we did not belong there. I politely let the woman know that we had reservations. She let us know that they were not ready and asked that we sit elsewhere until they were ready. My guest and i waited for about five minutes, then the hostess came back and let us know that our seats were ready. She explained that seats were assigned. She asked if our parking needed to be validated and I again politely let her know that we were guests here. My friends have also experienced odd behavior from staff when they visited the shops. They were made to feel uncomfortable as they browsed because the sales person followed them around the store, they never acknowledged them or asked if they needed help just followed them around as if they were going to steal something. I say all this to say that it is very hurtful and disrespectful to treat people this way. It shouldn’t matter what a person looks like or what their background is. The only race is the human race. We were guests at this resort and our experience has been soured. Since the tea we have just been in our room. We didn’t want to have to deal with being treated as less than. We wanted to go to the spa and the steakhouse but if I won’t be respected I don’t feel like I should spend anymore of my money. We were even given a 200 room credit as apart of our package as this was sponsored by our employer and we won’t be using the rest. Please address this with your staff and remember to treat everyone equally.

reviews.text: We love the Phoenician Residences! Over the last few years, it has become an annual destination for our family -- we look forward to escaping the cold winter weather for a week to spend thawing out at this resort. Over the years, we've stayed at the Phoenician, the Canyon Suites, and this year decided to try out the Phoenician Residences. Without a doubt: we will return!||||What we loved: ||(1) Staff. other than the check-in/check-out staff, which I've always found a bit wooden, we love the team at the Phoenician. From the concierge desk, to the kids club, to the restaurant staff, to the housekeeping team - they could not have been more lovely. Two examples: the concierge made a fantastic dinner recommendation nearby for a date night. At the restaurant, we were treated like royalty, including a couple of comp'd dishes and the manager swinging by to greet us. Housekeeping consistently kept attention to detail, from folding our PJs to leaving an extra shampoo when they realized we had used the full bottle one day. ||(2) Quality of the space. From the furniture to the beds to the outdoor grill, the Residences lived up to their name. Our family fully enjoyed having our own space with two bedrooms. One evening we even grilled out and enjoyed the patio.||(3) Service recovery. The A/C in our unit went kaput one evening. It was past the kids bedtime. The temperature was ticking up 78... 79 ... 81 ... An engineer hustled over. He worked his tail off to figure it out, up and down from the roof. He kept us super well informed. After an hour of tinkering, it was still not clear. We called the front desk, and after some hemming and hawing, the hotel juggled some rooms around and moved us right away. They sent someone down to help carry our stuff. While this was a huge pain for us to do a mini-repack and move (and we misplaced a few things in the shuffle!), the hotel handled it expediently. Kudos, especially to the sweating engineer!||(4) Grounds and amenities. They've done a few renovations and building over the years at the property. We've been fortunate to stay at many top tier properties around the world from Ritz Carltons to Park Hyatts to Four Seasons. From a physical build standpoint, the Phoenician is in that category. The new fitness facility is stunning. The spa facility is incredible and the team there was fantastic. The revamp of the lobby and restaurants are top notch -- after a lunch at Mowry & Cotton the day before we left, we actually wished we had eaten there more! Yum! I also loved how every Residence had its own golf cart with three rows. Since the Residences are set apart from the rest of the resort, it allowed us to zip up to the pools or the restaurants easily (and, hey, really fun too!).||(5) Nespresso machines and plentiful bottled water. Since I can't live without either of these, I was delighted to see both!! And the kitchens were equipped with cooking knives and utensils, table settings, toasters, can openers, chopping board, pots and pans, baking dishes and more. (Although in the midst of all that great provisioning, it was a little funny to see a cheap top/bottom fridge in 7004.) As noted above, we loved that the Residences had intimate outdoor areas with gas grills! We noted, but did not use, the outdoor fireplace in the ground floor Residences. They also had washer/dryers, which proved to be handy.||||What would have made it even more special:||(1) Titanium recognition. I don't make a big deal about this, but others do, so I'll mention it. There was none to speak of, really, beyond a "thank you" at check-in and the offer of breakfast credit or points. (And, unfortunately, the Phoenician falls into the group of hotels that just offer a breakfast benefit for Platinum/Titanium of yogurt+pastry+coffee, or $15 credit. So beware -- it is nitpicking the letter of Marriott benefits rather than extending a generous welcome like properties who provide Titaniums access to full buffets or anything off the menu. I'm also a Globalist at Hyatt and have never stayed at a Park Hyatt property where I was not offered a full breakfast buffet AND anything off the menu.) We were placed in Residence 7004 which was upstairs and was the only Residence without its own pool and just a hot tub. This actually was fine for us since we had toddlers and we really liked the layout of this particular Residence. I don't know if they consider the other Residences with their own pools as "upgrades" per se, but that was never offered. (We were moved to one due to our A/C issue. We actually liked 7004 layout better for our purposes, but I could see how a Titanium or Ambassador may expect to be placed in an upgraded Residence.)||(2) Proactiveness. This actually surprised me a bit. We had requested a crib in advance. I inquired at check-in since the kids were melting down in the car outside past their bedtime, but it was not in the Residence, even though we checked in after dinner time. The front desk agent called for it immediately and it was delivered within 30-45 minutes. Likewise on the service recovery, after interacting ourselves with the (very nice) engineer, we had to request a room exchange, rather than it being offered proactively. These are both super minor things, but being prepared for guests and anticipating needs are marks of leading hospitality.||(3) More as an FYI for other potential guests: the second bedroom is a King bed, like the master. I was a bit surprised they didn't appear to have a Residence or two with double beds in the second bedroom since I'm sure families would vastly prefer it.||||Overall, a fantastic stay and, as usual, when we check-out of the Phoenician we are sad to say "au revoir." The whole family is already looking forward to the next trip!! (In fact, already booked for 2020!)

reviews.text:
First time here for me - we arrived at 10am and they convinced us to take an "upgrade" to a residence rather than separate rooms. We were hesitant but said okay AS LONG AS it would be ready ASAP (i.e. cleaned immediately upon checkout) because we were already there and brought our dog, I.e. we couldn't go enjoy a lot of the resort spaces until our dog was set up in the room. We made it clear that just getting rooms early was our top priority.

6 HOURS later, and numerous conversations and phone calls later after leaving the property for lunch and then just basically sitting on benches waiting to get rooms and enjoy the resort, we are finally in our villa. reviews.text:
We were staying here as part of a Partners’ Retreat.
 
I received an email from The Phoenician on Thursday 7th March to download the Marriott Bonvoy app to enable us to check in faster, which I did. And on doing so I was asked for an estimated time of arrival and any room preference. I just asked for a king bed and feather pillows.
On arrival things were very smooth and our room was ready for us. Room number 2025 which was great, it was dark so we had no reason to look outside as we were due to join the event which had already started. In the morning we woke to find that our room faced a wall and there was hardly any natural light. We were extremely disappointed but thought at first that we would not be the only ones in the party.
It wasn’t until the Saturday evening when we were discussing rooms, everyone else we spoke to had really good views of the pools or golf course. I’m not entirely sure why we were given such a bad room especially when a one of the Partners I know arrived 2 hours after us had a villa with a view of the pool.
 
I have been to various Marriott resorts numerous time as my father has a timeshare of a 3 bedroom apartment at the Marbella Beach Resort, and has owned this since it was first built. (Around 20 years ago.) We generally always use Marriott hotels of some form and have never had such an awful view.
My partner and I were also considering purchasing a timeshare in the Marriott resort in Mallorca last year, but due to work commitments we decided to delay this until a later date.
 
The other issue we had was a late checkout. Our flight was not until 8.45pm and we wanted to use the pool for most of the day which was great. The facilities at the hotel are generally excellent and the staff are very good. We were only able to get a check out time up to 1pm and were told that we could use the facilities in the Golf/Fitness block.
While towels and showers (although with no apparent temperature gauge as they were scalding hot) were available, there was no hairdryer, which I have always seen in other Marriott resorts.

reviews.text: This resort is very well staffed and is clean and our stay was pleasant. It is quite expensive and there are added on fees (like the daily resort charge, house keeping, and parking) that added close to $100 per day to the cost. The restaurants were excellent, but again quite pricey. Needed reservation at the steakhouse when they saw that we had a child with us (though there were open tables) and Mowry and Cotton had slow service. Kids under 3 eat for free at Mowry and Cotton or for 1/2 price from age 3-12, but we had to ask for a correction to the bill every time for our petite 2 year old's meal. The resort is very close to Camelback Mountain trailhead, but the concierge was trying to discourage us from going...it was steep and rocky as we expected, but not that crazy of a hike since we're used to hiking the Cascades at home. This was a nice resort, but not very family friendly if you have a toddler. Probably better for school-aged kids. The included babysitting fee as part of the resort fee only covers kids over 5 yo, so we couldn't utilize it but were still charged $45/day for it.

Overall this is a nice resort.  However, there are not enough restaurants, it is impossible to get reservations and there are ZERO vegetarian/vegan options. We could not get tea reservations despite being there for 5 days.  There is no indoor pool except at spa, and the week was cold. There are few healthy options on the menus. Lots of meat and heavy foods.
The concierge was minimally helpful and usually too busy.  Check in was not smooth, we had to wait a long time for our room.
Service was slow at the breakfast place, despite it being mostly empty. 
They need more restaurants and indoor pool.  Concierge needs to be more attentive.
We did our own hiking and went to Sedona for a day, 1 hour 15 minute drive.  We were there over New Years for 5 days.
If you like quiet, this is a family resort, lots of children.  That was OK with us.
This would like to be a 5 star resort and it could be if fix the above problems. It is a 3-4 star at this point, despite 5 star prices.

Group Room Reservation
Front Desk
Meeting Concierge

reviews.text: When we checked in we tried to make Thanksgiving day dinner reservations. We had spent Thanksgiving there the year prior and really enjoyed our dinner at Mowry and Cotton. At the check in we were told that all the restaurants were full and we would have to go on a waiting list. We visited both restaurants (Plus 1 that was under construction) and supposedly got put on a list with our phone number. The day of Thanksgiving we decided to eat a late lunch at the pool since we probably weren't having dinner and we noticed that Mowry and Cotton was practically empty for their first seating at 2:30. Hmm. Never got that phone call. The pool manager listened to us vent and then was able to get us reservations for 7:30. We showed up at 7:30 and the restaurant was empty!  I have pictures to prove it. I cannot believe that 99% of the reservations were cancelled. I'm tired of talking about this so I'm stopping here even though there is more. Lets just say we were bitterly disappointed especially when you consider how much $$ we spent over the 4 days of our visit.

reviews.text:
We came for 4 nights of pampering and unfortunately experienced terrible service the entire stay.  My sister paid extra for a casita, but had a terrible view, a fire pit we couldn’t get to work, and they didn’t clean her room
2 of the 3 days (the third day the cleaned because she called to request cleaning).  Housekeeping didn’t clean my room the 3rd day and turndown service left melting ice cream sitting in my room.  The pool area at the end of the day was filthy and doesn’t get cleaned until morning- overflowing garbages, towels and used food and drinkware all over the place.
Food service took well over an hour at all 3 of the restaurants as well as room service.  The food quality was inconsistent. My nephews chicken was raw in the middle via room service.  I ordered a whiskey old fashioned at dinner one night and I’m pretty sure they used a salt packet instead of a sugar packet.  There was zero service at the pool, they were way understaffed (and pool area was only about 1/3 full)- one bartender was swamped trying to keep up with serving the entire pool.  The hotel is pretty, but perhaps a bit outdated- and not at all worth the price due to the bad service we received.  Truly one of the worst hotel experiences I’ve ever had.  Super bummed as we are two busy moms with young kids and don’t get a chance to get away frequently- this trip was a flop.

However, the spa facility is amazing.  So maybe next time I'll try a massage - as my husband enjoyed his massage.

reviews.text:
It's unfortunate that I have to do this but I need your help in sharing this message.

I'll start by stating I attached 3 photos that are pending approval. The photos are of the patio attached to the room I book at the Phoenician back in August. If approved I encourage you look for the images. I'll attempt to describe them below.

Imagine having a casual phone call in the middle of the night walking barefoot along your patio. Then in the morning when you retrace your steps you notice this filth. I say filth because my first assumption was not rodent droppings. Why are on earth would there be significant rodent droppings at a high quality resort? No, surely not rodent droppings.

I asked for second opinions from peers that were on the women's retreat that brought us Scottsdale what they thought of the filth. The consensus was "unspecified rodent droppings".

Upon checkout of our 2-night stay I noted the droppings, showing these same pictures to the receptionist at checkout. With the manager being off-site for the day they were unable to offer any sort of compensation, but referred us to email management. Afterwards questioning to the point of chastise why we didn't bring up the matter beforehand. (A workshop-filled retreat and the idealistic assumption that room service would include some type of evaluation of the patio were reason, but I digress.)

It is now October and management has not offered any sort of amends or compensation. In fact, their response rejects that the droppings came from a rodent but debris from a tree...you know the tree on the opposite side of the large cement wall that obstructs the view of trees.

I'm not in a habit of complaining. And I certainly don't appreciate being treated like a fool. The 5 women that witnessed the droppings on site, each an educated, cultured professional. One of the women works for another hotel chain that empowered me to speak up ensuring that most hotels attempt to rectify, not shame.

If you end up visiting the Phoenician Resort after this experience I suggest before you rest your head after a day of traveling, before you go eat because you may not have eaten all day, before you check in at whatever conference or event brought you to Scottsdale that you comb every inch of your room (both inside and out) because if you don't management will hold it against you.

... Also concerning is the unconfirmed tree-rodent (new species) infestation on garden level floors. I said "unconfirmed" because now I have to bring a lawyer into the situation. I'm no tree debris scientist, but wouldn't tree debris also be closer to the edge of a patio?
