As a Starwood member for many years I have accumulated lots of Starwood points and called the resort one week prior to my stay to inquire about using Starwood points to pay for various incidentals, meals etc. I was assured I would be able to be the front desk manager. When I got here I was told I couldn’t do to a “systems” issue and told to call corporate, who was also unhelpful. When I stressed that I would have stayed at one of the many other Marriott/starwood properties on site the front desk manager shrugged and appeared to have zero concern. reviews.text:
We recently stayed at the resort over the labor day weekend and I'm incredibly disappointed with the staff.  This post was 100% avoidable had any one of the 3 people I spoke with, on 3 separate days, simply called me back.  Long story short, my family and I checked out Monday (9/3) at 3pm, we have 2 childen so this process is always crazy and this is where the problems started, as I ended up leaving 3 headsets on the bench in the room.

As soon as we got home that night, I called the resort at 11:42pm CST, thinking that in order for me to maximize the chance of getting them back, we needed to get into the room quickly and/or talk to the employee(s) who cleaned the room.  The woman on the phone placed me on hold to talk to her lost and found department.  I told her that we needed to act quick, as I just checked out.  She told me the department is closed and she would call me back the next day, when they return.  I never received a call on 9/4 and so I called again on 9/5 at 1:21pm CST.  I spoke with a different woman who apologized profusely.  She was very sweet and I thought that I finally would be able to get some help.  She placed me on hold to speak with lost and found, again.   She returned and said they are not available but she would call me the next day.  I told her how time is not my friend here and we needed to get in contact with whomever cleaned the room after we left.  She told me that I was in luck because the room had a maintenance tag on it, which meant it was waiting for maintenance to go into the room and then it would be cleaned, so it wasn't even cleaned yet.  I told the woman that unfortunately I don't believe it wasn't entered by the housekeepers, because they knocked on our door around 2pm, to clean the room and we thought it was odd because we requested and was granted a 3pm check-out.  She again told me how she understood and said she was sending someone to the room immediately and I would receive a call back that day.  I never received a call that day or the next, so I called a final time on 9/7 at 12:23pm CST.  I again explained the entire story for a 3rd time, was placed on hold for lost and found, was told they weren't available and that I would receive a call back later in the day.  I asked to speak to a manager, she placed me on hold and then told me all managers are busy and they will call me back.

What do I do????  How could I have handled this differently? I tried 3 times, spoke with 3 different people and had the exact same result.  This is not a coincidence, this is how your people are trained.  I know it's my fault I left items in the room, I completely get that, but is this seriously how you train your people to react to guest issues?

We were and always are very generous with tipping the housekeepers daily, we are very generous with taking care of the other hotel employees as well.  We didn't request a discount or anything for free when our first room was infested with ants, we grabbed our stuff and just walked to the front desk.  No scene, no trouble.

So we respected everyone who directly or indirectly impacted our stay, why can't we get the same in return??

It can get very crowded and yet many seats go empty, because to reserve one of their prime deck spots (which are large decks of seats, not only cabanas) it will cost you $50 per seat. When paying a daily resort fee of almost $40/day with the tax, it seems outrageous to have to pay so much if you aren't out to the pool by noon. reviews.text:
Stayed at the Phoenician over the Labor Day weekend. Purchased 2 casitas for my family and my sisters family to celebrate the holiday weekend and our recent birthdays. Around 10 pm at night I noticed the water filling the sink and the bath tub were yellow tinted and dirty. Fortunately the front desk was able to move us to another room that was across a parking lot. Needing to rebath my children and myself we packed up our room, and carried our sleeping children to the new room.
When checking out the front desk manager was rude and since we had booked our rooms with Expedia, a third party, he was unable to make any consessions towards that rooms cost for the evening. I am not the type to complain about the few issues we encountered while staying at the property, but I was very surprised by the lack of courtesy the front desk manager had for our dirty water room, late night packing, moving rooms and my daughter becoming very upset that something was wrong with our room that could not be fixed. I am so disgusted by the fact that my family bathed, washed our face, brushed our teeth with dirty water at this resort. Our primary vacation due to my work, is staycation.... there is not a resort in Scottsdale/Phoenix/Tucson that we have not stayed at 5-3 stars.... skip this resort and go to the Hyatt at Gainey Ranch.... same family fun and entertainment.... clean water...

reviews.text:
Overall, nice hotel.

Rooms are well sized, the grounds are beautiful and spread out.

The staff is friendly and helpful.

The bathrooms are clean and well appointed.

There are several restaurants on the ground, but 2 key ones were closed during my stay in August, which made the restaurant options quite limited.

Food options are basically American food and seafood.

It would nice if they had a sushi restaurant.

The restaurant isn't walking distance to any other city ammenities, so plan on driving or taking a ride share service...

You're basically stuck in the hotel during your stay..

The pools are nice and the fitness gym is 24hrs which is very convenient...

There seems to be a lack of a basic mini-mart on the ground.. so getting access to bottled water without having to buy the expensive hotel bottled water was a challenge.

Restaurant prices are on the high side and the portions are slim.

Overall, a nice hotel for having functions  and company gatherings...

A good change from Las Vegas.

reviews.text:
Pleasant hotel and staff was remarkable! 

We chose Phoenician knowing it was not a "kid" resort however, we thought we would try it out given grand reviews and since our granddaughter (5) was joining us on this trip and reportedly there was a kid friendly area with water slide. That area needs major improvement, an adult cannot watch their child as there are NO chairs or places to sit around splash pad or slide. In my opinion, it promotes unsupervised child chaos which can potentially be unsafe for little ones.

reviews.text:
Just returned from my stay and had a subpar experience. There was a lack of follow up, and service was slow on some days. Seemed the hotel was understaffed.



I was given an upgrade, but it was mainly to free up a room for the conference that was taking place there. We were in a room further away from the pool with a fire pit in August and were told that was an upgrade. It was 114 degrees outside!



On the weekend, the pool was so packed that it took about 15 minutes to get food/drinks, and it took us about 30 minutes to get our bill. We had to walk up to the bar ourselves to close out. The front desk apologized and offered a credit that was never applied. I had inquire about the credit at the front desk the day we checked out. They told me they would take care of it only to receive a carbon copy of the original receipt with no credit and had to call again from the airport. I received my final bill with the credit and a new charge the next day. It was confusing, so I called with questions and was told by one person that it would be adjusted. I then received a follow up phone call from the manager who only called to tell me there would be no credit and the invoice was correct after I was just told the invoice was not correct. Their lack of training and lack of communication led to a misunderstanding and frustration on my part. My frustration and confusion was met with attitude by the manager. At that point, you just please the customer and move on. This hotel acts like they are doing you a favor by taking your money. 



The pools were great, the fitness center was excellent, and the spa was nice, but the service at the front desk was awful, the food was subpar, and the room was just ok.



I would not recommend this resort to any of my friends.

The worst customer service.
I tried to purchase a gift card for a coworker.
Part of it on a company card and part on my personal card. Straight forward numbers nothing complicated.
First time they charged my card an amount way over what the 2 charges combined were supposed to be. And then “apologized” and put my account in the negative. Went all weekend with no access to my funds. By the way, the electronic transaction has to be done by a manager and even stated the amounts on the 2 forms filled out. They still couldnt figure it out.
Then my business card was charged twice, 2 different amounts. THEN once my refund cleared and I allowed them to try again but made sure we quadruple checked the very straight foward amount for each card... they charged my personal card twice causing yet another issue with my account.
All I got was an I am so sorry about that Ms. Gilbertson.
Honestly I don’t want the gift card, if you cant manage to charge my cards right I really am not interested in gifting anyone a massage when it could potentially be yet another disaster.
Waiting on you to give me my money back.

reviews.text: The Phoenician has never looked better - the rooms and public areas are modern and stylish. However we did have a few unpleasant problems during our stay and the hotel didn't seem terribly interested in correcting them in any way. When we opened the sofa bed we discovered that the sheets were not clean. It was too late at night for my sleepy son to care but I did report the problem the next day (nothing was done other than an apology). Just before leaving we discovered a very lively roach in the room. I reported it to the front desk and again nothing was offered in terms of compensating us for that. I understand these things can happen in a hotel but usually management cares a bit more. The pool area has a ridiculous policy of charging to sit in an enormous area. As a result, there was not a single person sitting in that area and all the paying hotel guests were seated in other areas that weren't quite as pleasant.

reviews.text: My wife and I thoroughly enjoyed our stay at The Phoenician. We have stayed there many times before in the past but this was our first day since the remodel. In general it was an excellent stay, five star. A few things that could have been improved though were the restaurant situation. With J&G closed and Il Terrazzo now converted to another restaurant, choices of restaurants on the property are Limited The menu was very limited at Mowrie and Cotton, and the Relish Burger Bar is a bit of a walk from the hotel. The other issue has to be with the outside new pool bar. It completely blocks off the view of anyone on the right side of the upper floors of the hotel. It's a lot of money to pay to stay up there to look at the roof or back of a building. Other than that it's the same old Phoenician with the A+ service. They did do a great job relocating the Thirsty Camel bar to become the centerpiece of the lobby overlooking the windows in the valley. The old Thirsty Camel was sort of crammed into one of the back rooms which now looks to be the Tea Room. The new bar is the centerpiece of the lobby and really pulls it all together. It also seems like with the remodel upstairs the bathrooms seem to have lost perhaps a foot or more of space. Still very spacious but doesn't quite seem to be the same size as the old Phoenician prior to the remodel. For golfers the golf course is now closed under serious renovation. They also built a brand new exercise Center which looks great along with the new spa and rooftop pool that we can get a chance to try.

reviews.text:
We stayed at The Phoenician for a staycation while our son was at camp in northern Arizona. We were expecting a great time as we’ve stayed at plenty of great luxury resorts. The service is always great at SPG/Marriott, but, we were blown away by the staff at The Phoenician. From the reception staff to the pool serving staff - everyone was a delight. 



What we weren’t expecting was the amazing service at the pool bar with Kris. He made us feel welcome and went above and beyond what was expected. We ended up extending our stay not once - but, twice - mostly attributed to him. He gets it and is an expert in creating not only a remarkable experience but one you want to tell everyone about. Thanks, Kris!

reviews.text:
We've been married 42 years, but never had a honeymoon. This was the honeymoon worth waiting for. Everything was perfect plus, plus, plus. The food at Mowry & Cotton was the best restaurant food we've ever had, by far. All fresh, all incredibly creative and all very healthy besides! The pheasant and ribs are out of this world and every breakfast was an exciting adventure, the crab omlet and Buddha bowl may be our favorites, but it would be worth going back for another 6 days just to try more of the fabulous things on the menu.

The service was again beyond any expectations: gracious, every request immediately responded to with always even more than what we'd asked for, the utmost efficiency and professionalism, combined with thoughtful kindness from every single staff person we encountered. "Excellence on every level," as my husband put it.

Besides all that, everything is either brand new or just newly totally rennovated. The 6 or 7 (we lost count) pools are all beautiful, water pristine, perfect temperature, colored with lights under the water at night....a fabulous jaccuzi....great, impromptu, anticipate-your-every-need pool service for everything, etc.

The whole place is also huge, with spacious, very beautifully landscaped grounds and convenient paths, so a great place to walk around in too. The totally new work out area is state-of-the-art amazing. The 2 acre cactus garden is stuning, especially for midwesterners, who have not seen 15 foot cacti standing in front of them along lovely winding paths, studded with striking statues, scultures and monuments (all over the grounds too).

We truly cannot say enough good about this resort and are so happy we stayed there. If you get the chance, do go there. It's also lovely for children, with a whole new water area of special children's attractions, besides the other pools.

All in all our experience at the Phoenician was beyond our wildest expectations. Just so fine!

reviews.text: I spent a day at the newly their remodeled spa yesterday. It was beyond 5 star! Being a local, I have gone to this spa since it opened 20+ years ago and it was always was one of my favorites. What they created is a world class spa. It ticks all the boxes in what you would want in a spa: steam room, sauna, jacuzzi, rooftop pool with delicious food and impeccable service, quiet room where you can lay down and nap or just relax, nuts, chocolate, tea, ice water complimentary in the relaxation room, huge spaces beautifully decorated and giving you a feeling of relaxation and serenity. I had the Salt Stone treatment and it was over the top. For lunch I had the vegetarian kabob, it was delicious and enough for 2 people. The only thing missing is clocks!  I never knew what time it was and always needed to look at my iphone so I wouldn't miss my treatment time. If you go, plan to spend the day and enjoy all the amenities.

reviews.text: I chose the Phoenician as I expected a flawless experience to celebrate my daughter's milestone birthday. When I booked this property I was not told that it was under MAJOR construction and therefore major inconvenience, noise and limited amenities, Since we were on the spa package, I tried to book spa appointments and I found out that the spa was not even open as they were moving to the new facility that was far from complete. By the end of the week we were able to get basic services but many services were not available including steam, sauna, pool etc. They did not even have a menu of services so we were not aware of the newly inflated prices or that 20% gratuity was included! They gladly accepted the additional 25% tip that I left. They should be embarrassed at what they call their fitness facility. The pools were overcrowded with kids, no different than what you would find at a Disney resort. Our room wasn't even cleaned 2 days in a row even though we were out of the room at 8:30am and didn't return until dinnertime. Service at the restaurant was pretty bad and birds were feasting on uncleared tables. Corporate events were being catered to and the average guest just got lost in the shuffle. Yoga mats were never cleaned and there were no towels provided for us to wipe down our own mats. Poor communication in all respects. No peacefulness as construction was everywhere. No break on price either even though this place was heavily under construction with several amenities unavailable and extremely noisy. This experience was a far cry from the flawless experience I had there several years ago. We will never go back as this is not the Phoenician that has the stellar reputation.

reviews.text:
Being a SPG platinum Residence owner at the St Regis, I was disappointed to get my SPG breakfast ONLY when I inquired about it.

I don’t think I have ever not been offered it upon check in. I felt it was intentional that points were put on my account without asking me which I would prefer.

This was after waiting in a

We really wanted to love our second visit to the Phoenician — unfortunately the luxury aspirations the resort has did not measure up. I will start with the positive — rooms are spacious (we stayed in the Canyon Suites), grounds are well kept and our 6 year old daughter loved the counselors at the kids club. Opportunities for improvement include:

(1) inconsistent wait service — we visited the pools 2/day during our 5 day stay. At least once daily, we were invisible to wait staff for service. 

(2) add on fees — $25 for “reserved” pool chairs is inconsistent with peer respect chains and not aligned with the luxury brand aspirations 

(3) subpar gym for “luxury” resort. Not enough equipment as people waited to get on machines



Sadly we won’t be returning.

reviews.text:
Upon check in, we asked for reservations at Relish. The individual took my cell phone and said he'd call me with a reservation confirmation. He did not do so, so we went down to the front desk to express our frustration. A different individual at the front desk then apologized and said he'd call over right away. When we arrived, the hostess said she did not receive a call. She checked everyone in the bar, etc. and they did not receive a call either. We have 2 small children and had to wait a long time to eat. 

The air condition on the roof was so loud....like a squeeling chopper... it would only stop when the air condition would go on. Our family had a rough time sleeping.

Lastly, I requested a late check out when I reserved the room, and upon my arrival. They said I couldn't confirm until the morning of. We called down at 7AM, and they did not accommodate us even though we had an evening flight. I feel this treatment was to us using our well deserved points for the room. We should not be treated any different than "non point" guests. We spend a lot of money at the resort during our stay.

reviews.text:
The Phoenician is a wonderful hotel and has the best of just about every amenity - service, room quality, staff, housekeeping, etc. I am writing this review because I could not find anywhere on the website to e-mail management directly.

I stayed in this hotel from March 28 -April 2 with two rooms. On the third night, I ordered room service and, among other things, had the flatbread. Later that night and the entire next day, I was vomiting profusely and had diarrhea. This had to be caused by the hotel food as I didn't leave the hotel since arriving three days before and had only eaten hotel food. That was also the the only thing I had eaten that day. After feeling better two days later, I ordered the chicken shishkabob for my kids by the pool. As I cut the chicken for my kids, I noticed it wasn't cook thoroughly and had pink/red inside. When I brought this up to the waitress, the person behind me (last name Hull) told me that he had the same problem two days ago and was sick.

If you want to remove this post, you can. I am not litigious, not a complainer, was not looking for any apologies/compensation when this happened (nothing the hotel can do when one has food poisoning), not a complainer, nor am I writing this review to scare anyone. I understand that these things sometimes happen (I was born in the restaurant business). However, I just want management to be aware of this so it does not happen to anyone else. For the cost of this hotel per night, this should not happen.

Otherwise, the hotel is an A+ and I have spent over 1000 nights in SPG and Marriott properties as I travel often.

reviews.text:
Just checked out from a generally underwhelming stay at The Phoenician. I've long wanted to stay at this property, given its reputation as a luxury experience, and decided to splurge on a birthday weekend for my mom.



From check in to check out, the experience was ... blah. Not what I would expect from a property of this caliber. And definitely not worth the cost - save your splurge for somewhere else, or stay at the downtown Westin (my personal favorite) and spend your money on theater tickets, meals out, and shopping!



A few things:

-We only received turndown service 1 of 2 nights.

-Poor early afternoon and late night dining options. Nowhere to relax with a drink before 2 pm, unless you want a restaurant or the pool. Nighttime food is incredibly limited, and the live music in the bar area is so loud that ordering a drink from the bartender is impossible, let alone having a conversation with a companion.

-Ditto for the coffee shop. If you can't snag one of the handful of outdoor tables, forget about drinking your coffee and reading the paper, given the absolutely blaring music.

- Signage throughout the property is terrible, a must for a resort of this size. Four different staff members gave us four different set of directions to the fitness center. Signs were of absolutelty no assistance, as they were conflicting, as well.

-Once we arrived, the temporary fitness center was terrible. I can completely understand that construction requires making accommodations, but not sacrifices in equipment quality (could have found a better treadmill at a garage sale) or cleanliness (garbage and dirty towels on the floor).

-Service was generally good. Some real superstars, while others, again, are not at the level expected of a property like The Phoenician.

-Rooms are clean and comfortable.

reviews.text:
I will begin by saying we travel quite extensively and that I usually am quite happy when we book luxury accommodations. However, I have to say that our experience this weekend with this resort was ho hum. We have been to Scottsdale many times and always stayed at another nearby Scottsdale resort. But this time we hoped to step it up a notch and pamper ourselves for my birthday weekend. 



From the checkin to checkout, we never felt welcomed or pampered. Our room was the furthest from the lobby and on the ground floor facing the mountain. The outdoor garden is beautiful but we felt like we were in a cave. When I booked, I requested a balcony and a fire pit. We received neither. The porch only had one chair to sit on and it was far to chilly to sit outside without a warm fire or a propane heater. 



At the pool, we were not welcomed or given towels for over 1/2 hour. The only reason why we were even addressed was to tell us that we were sitting in an area reserved for those paying for cabanas, even though we were in front if it with no signage stating this. Due to weather, that was the only day we even tried the pool area. 



We parked our rental car in the garage. Each time we tried to enter or leave, our card didn’t work. We would have to press the button and wait for someone to answer. No one ever picked up! Not one time. 



We decided to give the Burger restaurant a try. Asking the concierge where it was, we were told to hike down to the golf club. This was a significant distance down through the pool complex and steps. It was windy and chilly. Upon arriving, there was a sign stating that the restaurant was closed today. No explanation! Why didn’t the concierge tell us? Hiked back up and got in the car and drove over to our familiar resort for dinner which was warm, welcoming and friendly and features live music every night. We heard no live music at any time during our stay. 



Checkout gave me a near heart attack when I tried to check out via my room tv. It had doubled my bill! I was late leaving for the airport because I had to go to the front desk to check out to resolve the problem. I was told...oh we have a problem with that system! Really? When you pay this much for a hotel, you expect the correct bill and online checkout.



I believe this resort is great if you are looking for a nice conference center but I would call it cold, plastic and not welcoming. I am an SPG member but I am not coming back any time soon. Too bad because we love resorts like this!

Imagine paying this much, and turning on the shower in the morning, and having little stray sprays going all over and not getting a full refreshing stream. This affected my casitas in both P and O. It sounds like a small detail, but it sticks out like a sore thumb. So easy to solve, I've never encountered this at a good hotel anywhere in the world. Other than that, I would only comment that some room views are fantastic -

 valley, garden and grass, while other room views are terrible, like parking lot and roads. So, there should be a real big variance in price and a full disclosure at reservation time; but there isn't. At the time we booked, we thought the gym and spa would be complete in December, but they're behind schedule. The new lobby area is fantastic; we had drinks there every day at happy hour. The cactus garden was lit with Christmas lights, simply gorgeous. There are many activities on property for families. The service on the days leading up to Christmas when the hotel wasn't full was spectacular. Unfortunately, when the hotel filled up on Christmas, the staff was inexplicably unprepared and as a result, from then on, the service at the pool was poor and there were long lines at the restaurant for breakfast despite that at least half the patio tables were open. They also made a mistake with the late check out (ie confirmed it the night before departure, and then that morning said there was no late check out booked). reviews.text: Unfortunately, myself, along with my colleagues had a number of experiences relating to poor service. I was hoping the experience at dinner (J&G Steakhouse) was a one off, but in all honesty, the lack of customer service was prevalent throughout the hotel, which was extremely disappointing. To summarize, it appears the hotel service sector (food and beverage) was poorly staffed and lacked the ability to provide the basic customer service standards, i.e., taking our order, refilling water, bringing the bill, being attentive, bringing the wrong drinks and food.... You name it and it happened. We complained to the front desk, who showed signs of concern, however, we never received any formal feedback from the management. While most of the staff was friendly, the hotel lacks the quality to ever be ranked higher than a 3 star, in my book. In addition, the rooms were comfortable, but felt cheap. If you do consider staying at this hotel, I would recommend eating offsite.

reviews.text: We did an extended family vacation here and it was fantastic. We knew going into it that there was ongoing construction of the new spa and sports facility, as well as a kiddie area. The work detracted from the relaxation atmosphere a tiny bit, but that's temporary. The rooms were very comfortable, the staff in all areas was responsive and nice and happy to help. There seemed to be a lot new staff on board, training, so the experience wasn't quite up to standards of other 5 star resorts, but I'd stay here again in a few months when everything should be settled. The pool area was super relaxing, safe with kids but not loud as one might expect with lots of families. The restaurants were tasty across the board. Loved happy hour on the outdoor balcony, fun classes included, great fitness and tennis even if temporary. Location fantastic - so nice to hike Camelback Mountain within walking distance. Commend the hotel on their falconry program!! It was one of our favorite things about the stay - Mark and John were fantastic with guests, even while doing their main job - handling the hawks. We interacted with them daily. Lots for kids to do. I plan to stay here again and highly recommend.

reviews.text:
We arrived with two small children. We requested a crib and unfortunately we had to ask three times to receive the crib. 



Our luggage took almost 2 hours to arrive. 



The front desk staff was not knowledgeable on facility activities or local dining reccommendations. The bare minimum. 



We had to call 3 different times/ people to book a hotel experience. (One that we paid additional to attend) before confirming reservations. 



We booked this resort because of the “kids activities and children’s pool/ swimming options”. The kids pool was closed. New kids area under construction, but we would have booked another hotel had we known this information. 



We had multiple problems with housekeeping. Asked for service many times daily. Service still lacking when they finally came. 



Finally, when we were leaving, the front desk agent Jordan asked about my stay. I politely said that we had some issues that were frustrating. Not only did she not apologize, she did not even ask what the issues were. How can you improve on something when you don’t ask for information. This is the first and only negative hotel review I️ have written. 



I️ would have been happy if the staff would have offered something. Anything. Pay for parking? Anything. It’s not about the money. The hotel is expensive and we dined in the facility and took part in special event offers. It’s about having a bad experience and no one seeming to care. The staff needs training. Period. 



I️ hate writing such a negative review, but I️ hope this will help others to make a different choice. 



Best, 



Lisa

The food was a little disappointing did not have any knock out meals,we tried every restaurant on the resort also room service,so so.
reviews.author: Midi

reviews.text: My friends and I had the pleasure of visiting the Phoenician this November for a 4 day girls getaway. The property is beautiful and staff extremely attentative. The concierge helped us set up everything from dinner reservations to spa appointments to giving us water before our hike on camelback ! The on-site restaurant Mowry and Cotton has the absolutely most delicious breakfast menu and dinner will also not disappoint ! Highly recommend this hotel for any type of stay (girls getaway, family, business). Look forward to coming back soon.

reviews.text: Beautiful wedding venue

reviews.text: Great hotel. Beautiful views. Great pool. Awesome rooms.
reviews.author: Jill Wilson

reviews.text: We stayed in Casita 7175 from 10/29/17 to 10/31/17 and it was far from a Luxury experience. First, due to construction at the resort you can not access the casita parking from the main entrance and must leave the resort and re-enter from the Golf/Tennis entrance which is approximately 1 mile away. Second, the gates to enter this part of the resort were padlocked closed at 9:00pm on Sunday and we were informed that we needed to drive around, park in the garage and walk to our room. The room itself is lacking in many aspects: (1) it took a minimum of 7-10 minutes for hot water to arrive at either the shower or tub each time we attempted to use them, (2) the air conditioning “cycles” on/off every 3 to five minutes and due to the positioning of the vents blows directly onto the bed with such force that you can sit or sleep. (3) finally, some notice should be given regarding the construction and the 7:00am start. The pool area and food at Relish were good and enjoyable. I would not recommend the Casita’s at this property to anyone but the stay in the Hotel may be a better experience.
reviews.author: HoustonStrong

reviews.text: Recently ate a fantastic brunch on the patio at Mowry & Cotton. The view was beautiful, and the food was amazing.
reviews.author: Becky Hoffmann

reviews.text:
The Marketplace is a hidden gem. Great stop when cycling through PV or just for a coffee stop. The pastries are really worth the trip (although they are hidden from view, make sure you walk out the interior door to see the display!)
Service is great and there are tables to sit at. So nice!
reviews.author: Leslie Campbell

reviews.text: Love this place, especially since the recent renovations.  Yes it had gotten rather down at the heels in prior years, with carpets and cushions showing wear, and postponed maintenance.  But the layout of the pools, grounds and the size of the rooms kept us coming back year after year.  Now since the facelift it's that much more attractive.  Prices are up accordingly, but you get what you pay for.
reviews.author: Alex Hamilton

reviews.text: Beautiful environment in every way! Pool so luxurious... dessert garden fantastic . Room was fantastic ... quiet . Comfortable ... very clean. Loved the way my room was tidy every night ... even wrapping my phone cords! Bath was delightful. Meals were great ! We have breakfast with a meeting but all the provided meals were fantastic . Also fined at malery and cotton .. great food ! Such clean healthy choices! Very inspiring . Group hikes by Grayson also much fun!
reviews.author: Catty75

reviews.text: I'll be coming back same time next year to relax and enjoy the amenities. Scottdale is a wonderful town with a lot of healthy and fun people to meet and party with all night long. I highly recommend https://steak44.com and the many cigar bars in and around the city. Golf, Tennis and pools all immaculate. Treat yourself and stay a couple of weeks. You won't regret it.

reviews.text: I've stayed at 5 Starwood / Marriott properties in Scottsdale. The Phoenician is my favorite. Big beautiful rooms and bathrooms.

reviews.text: Beautiful
reviews.author: Max Kol

reviews.text: We have stayed at many SPG Hotels and the Phoenician does fit the Luxury category. The rooms are well appointed and spacious. The Room direction to the sun definitely effects the room and terrace so should be noted to guests. Excellent lobby bar with modern and spacious indoor and outdoor seating and superior service. Restaurants are also excellent (including afternoon tea), but should not close the main resturant for all day type dining in the afternoon. The pools are very nice and spacious with an adult only section and also excellent service. The spa is under renovation right now but does have limited services. Very convenient to shopping and area attractions.
reviews.author: Missica

reviews.text: This is a beautiful facility with an excellent staff, well schooled in customer service and attention to detail. I had a few minor issues with housekeeping and the pool area. I wasn 't informed that there was turndown service so I neglected to remove the do not disturb sign the first night we were there. Our housekeeper mistakenly discarded my aluminum water bottles I left on the dresser to dry. No one cleaned nor restocked the coffee maker until I had to notify the front desk. I did not appreciate being told I couldn't sit in certain pool areas that were reserved for "VIP", code for pay $25 to reserve a lounge. This seems to me to be gouging. Those aside, we had an enjoyable stay.

reviews.text:
Everything here is 5 star from the staff to the grounds to the amenities.
Very pleasant and helpful people, very clean and newly updated rooms.
Not a bad drive from Phoenix airport

It looks like it will be another year or two before it will become a relaxing place to vacation. Very unfortunate, we were led to believe everything except the spa was complete. Not even close to being accurate.

reviews.text: From the moment I walked into this beautiful resort, I knew I was going to have a great, relaxing time. You can tell by the actions of the employees that they go above & beyond for the guests. Room was beautiful and clean (with a solid view of Camelback Mountain). The resort is massive, so it'll take a little while to have the entire area covered. Food was delicious through room service as well as the food joints they offered on property. I would recommend this to anyone of all ages to go, relax, unwind & forget about responsibilities for a while. Whenever I find myself back in Arizona, I'll be sure to come back here.

I think the biggest thing that stands out is how their staff has always treated me with the same respect and welcoming attitude, whether I arrived in a VW Bug in the 90s for my high school senior trip or in recent years for weekend getaways with my husband. I can't wait to see what the latest evololution will add to what is already my favorite escape.

When I tried to call the front desk my calls would either go to a different hotel or it would take them forever to answer my call. reviews.text:
All the websites pool pictured areas were under construction and the small pool that was available for use was too small and inconvenient. The brick around the pool was HOT and burned our feet so we had to wear flip flops before stepping in the pool. 



Spa service, this was in a hotel room because that area was also under construction. Spa service was good. 



Breakfast on the 5th floor was ridiculously expensive, over $60 for 2 people, food was not worth the money. 



Bathroom door wouldn't close, it needed adjustment. Toilet kept running, but was fixed the next day. Room temp control on went to 67 degrees, we had to call maintenance to lower the temp. Our room view was ok so long as you ignored the construction. 



Front desk and Pool staff was friendly, especially Brian, the pool guy. Burgers, wings and tots were delicious. Hotel was beautiful and room was spacious, especially with 2 queen beds.

We made the reservation base on pictures we saw on the website( the pool for my wife) and decided to visit this place. Got an email from the hotel that they was under construction and had limited access to things at the hotel.I believe a week after we made the reservation, Called the hotel and asked and was only told about the hotel rooms and construction work around the hotel. Nothing about the pool or shops closed. 

The pool was closed and they had this made up pool that looked like a YMCA pool. Other people at the pool was complaining as well. 

No places to shop for anything

Not one employee went out of there way! Not on!

The food choices are also limited and I tend to go out, rather than eat at the hotel. The hotel bar is small and boring.

reviews.text:
I took several couples to the Phoenician and was excited when I made the reservations. I had been there years ago and remembered it to be a 5 star property.



We booked rooms under a Spa package deal, but ended up getting significantly overcharged because of the billing system they use. The system could not recognize our package and ended up charging us ala carte for everything. When I tried to resolve it with accounting, they were no help and even the hotel's management would not help. I ended up paying much more than the package suggested.



The spa was fine and the food was good, but the hotel appears to be mismanaged and the billing is uncoordinated within the property.



It ended up being a nightmare situation that the hotel would not help me resolve. I'll never go back, and would not recommend it.



Interestingly, when I was at the front desk on 4 separate occasions trying to get the billing straightened out, I heard quite a few other guest who were also complaining about their hotel bills. Apparently I wasn't the only one getting overcharged. There are quite a few other Spa Resorts in Phoenix. I would try another one if I were you! The Phoenician isn't worth the headache and hassle.

reviews.author: Michael Stevens

reviews.text:
Beautiful tennis facilities, kind staff, private atmosphere. Any time spent at The Phoenician is guaranteed to please and relax. The evening ambiance is characterized by mild temperatures and light breezes.

I chose to sit outside, with nothing to do. I could not focus, for the life of me, on the book I had brought for myself to read. The sunset views from the golf and tennis facilities totally captivated my imagination.

You can feel the history here. Those short hours spent in the evening breeze took me back to a most unique frame of mind. One can almost taste the nuclear ambitions of a 1950's America at The Phoenician, where even today, at the crossroads of opulence & comfort, the tastefully landscaped grounds offer any visitor an enriching experience.
reviews.author: Cale Haug

reviews.text: Despite all of the renovations taking place at the resort during our stay, the staff did an incredible job at not skipping a beat. Everyone was very helpful, happy to be there, and always trying to make our stay better wherever possible. I was slightly skeptical about staying there with so many renovations going on, but due to the staff it made everything better. Way to go!

Once there it's a hole with water in it, think back yard rectangular vinyl lined pool with brick pavers around it. Seriously hot on the feet have your flip flops sitting next to where you enter the pool you will need them to  get back to your Lounge.  Half of the golf is closed sorry golfers. On the up side very few people staying here so it quite! Relish Burger Bistro makes a mean burger imo best eats on the entire resort. Parking is easy lots of spaces. reviews.text: Although the resort has potential it fell short of satisfactory. When we arrived at the resort we found out that the pool was closed for renovations but a  tennis court had been used to turn into a pool area and now this is the only pool they have to offer during renovations.  I was extremely disappointed that I was not notified before hand.  Also the main Spa had been closed for renovations. However another spa had been opened for renovations.  Sorry but after seeing the tennis court turned into a pool for renovations I didn't want to see what the spa looked like.  The staff was super apologetic but unfortunately  was a too little too late.  Although we still made the best of it and had a great time in Phoenix,  we were still very disappointed in our hotel stay.  Also there were several pictures of different restaurants the hotel was supposed to have that are also close to renovations.  I definitely think this will be a great hotel to stay at but would wait till after renovation come fall 2017

reviews.text: To be honest, our stay warrants 3 stars or less, but I'm giving four, because I know it's not typical, and our issues are only temporary problems that don't deserve a permanent bad review. Still pretty annoyed, though... See, when we booked our stay, we were not made aware that a large portion of the amenities were under renovation. We packed our swimsuits expecting the beautiful pool and splash pad (for our daughter) featured in pictures of the resort to be available. We didn't find out until check-in that all the amenities we planned on were under renovation. Not only this, but the main entrance to the hotel was also under renovation, so we had to use a side entrance that forced us to walk... and walk... and walk... to our room that was almost literally the furthest away we could have been. Arriving late at night with a sleeping infant and 2-year-old who both needed to be carried back to our room was a huge pain because of this. Our walk would have been almost cut in half had the main entrance to the hotel been available. We were not offered anything to make up for the inconvenience, and the only reason we continued our stay was because my husband's company had already paid for our room, and we had plenty we wanted to do off the hotel property anyway. All that said, the hotel and resort are lovely and well kept, the rooms are very nice, and the beds were very comfortable. Had the resort not been under renovation, I'm sure it would have been a perfect stay.

reviews.text:
We had the pleasure of staying at the Phoenician Hotel in Scottsdale Az on its last weekend before it begins a major remodel. I have never been to this property before and was very excited to see and experience it. As Forbes and AAA Five Star Five Diamond Trained Customer Service expert, it's hard to not always have my eyes on every attention to detail. I felt the communication upon arriving lacked a little. The check-in process needs to be easier for those staying in a Casita, or simply asking your guests are they staying with us, rather than "are you self-parking or valet" It was just a bit confusing and inconvenient. Next- I find it completely ridiculous that a 300 Acre Hotel in the middle of the desert where I am on the OFF Season finds a reason to charge people for parking. What an easy luxury that could be avoided, or included already in the rooms price. No one wants extra fees. 

We upgraded our room specifically to a Casita for a fire pit. When looking online it shows these rooms, but does not say that the second floor Casitas do not have a fire pit. We did not get one. The room itself was incredibly beautiful, despite the spider in the bath tub. The bed could not have been more comfortable. 

I thoroughly enjoyed all of the pool amenities and service. As well as all of my dining service experiences at Relish, Thirsty Camel, and Il Terrazzo. Ericka- from Thirsty Camel, was especially hospitable. 

We had a very short stay and initially asked for a late check out. Upon checking in the Gentlemen next to me received this benefit and I wanted to as well. We were initially denied that perk and told to call back in the morning. I understand and empathize with this industry, but it does seem suspicious for me to witness a service being provided to one person and then have it quickly denied to me. We were granted a 1 hour delay check out the next morning when I woke up and called the front desk. Which, I was grateful for. 

We had an amazing opportunity to attend the final guided mediation class in The Center for Well-Being Spa. We really enjoyed this experience, the service of the Spa, and all its amenities. 

 All in all. We left happy despite feeling snubbed in some ways, I would still recommend this beautiful property and look forward to seeing it when the remodel is complete.

reviews.text: I visited the Phoenician as a guest of one of their third-party vendors. The Phoenician is beautiful, great pools, great entertainment. One of the vendors coworkers was out that day comma so there was one person managing all of their equipment. At the end of our activity, the third party vendor was looking for someone at the Phoenician to assist with her equipment, and none were willing. After waiting 20 minutes on a golf cart they said she could borrow, another employee said they are not available to help third-party vendors with the carts. The lower pool bar was WAY under staffed and the bartenders were clearly stressed out. The trip was topped off with a AC problem that woke my wife and I up at 4AM. the T-stat was set at 65 degrees and the room temp was 77, a temp that was uncomfortable and left us both pretty miserable in the AM. reviews.text:
We recently stayed at the Phonecian and our stay was just fine. No major issues or concerns, however I was a little surprised that for a place that bills themselves as luxury that the stay was just that. Overall I would say the service was inconsistent. Again not bad, just inconsistent and less than one may expect if you've stayed at other luxury properties.



The pool staff was pretty understaffed, took quite a bit of time to get chairs set up (if you could find a chair at all) drinks were even slower. It seemed as if there was only one bartender for all pools - frozen drinks were not so frozen by the time you received them. 



One morning I called at about 7:30a.m. one morning for more coffee pods for our room. (I drink decaf) at least two hours later they still hadn't arrived - only to just be refilled by the housekeeping staff when our room was cleaned that day. Again, this was fine....but I had actually wanted to drink more coffee that morning - not later that day. 



Our newspapers can the first few mornings and we're just left outside the door. The remainder of the trip they were put into a nice bag and hung on the door. Not an issue, again just inconsistent in the approach/level of service detail.



On a positive note our 21 month old son loved the pools. Was great there was a splash pad and small wading pool. He spent hours and hours in both! 



Overall these aren't necessarily reasons that we wouldn't return or recommend to others as it worked for what we needed for this particular stay but just a few things that could use a little improvement to make the experience a little better.

reviews.text:
While the beauty and elegance of this hotel stands out above the rest, the staff/services was nothing short of disappointing. 



From the first point of check-in I was disappointed to not have been offered any sort of bonus options and was literally just told "here is your key and there are the elevators, be sure to wear this neon green bracelet around the hotel". The bracelet was nothing short of annoying and gave the feeling that this was more of a club than a resort; I ripped it off that night.



During my actual stay I attempted to sit poolside but was never actually able to. At approximately 7am 95% of all the pool chairs were covered in guests items in order to reserve them for the day. Disappointingly there are signage that says not to do this and your items will be removed but when I asked multiple staff members about this I received conflicting answers and essentially was told "too bad". I understand that staff is not looking for an altercation but then I suggest removing the signage that says you will do so and re-train your staff to follow the same guidelines as it is frustrating to hear one thing from the concierge and another from the pool manager (Mario).



Once they did place additional chairs on the south lawn I was able to get a seat but then it became nothing short of a chore to get the staff to pay attention to us. It seems that the lawn receives lackluster service when compared to the pool and any drinks ordered will be served melted (if frozen) or warm. The food itself was even more disappointing, nothing fresh to choose from and cooked poorly.



To top everything off my room was only cleaned two out of the four days that I was present. I assumed that I must have indicated that I did not way it cleaned and would be receiving some benefits for not having it cleaned, but no I did not.



The positives were that hotel was clean,beautiful and had large rooms but unfortunately the negatives like not having my room cleaned, the lackluster staff and disappointing SPG rewards outweighed the positives here.
